results.question: Under what conditions can a UE supporting WUS assistance include its UE paging probability information during an attach or tracking area updating procedure?
results.reference: The UE can include its UE paging probability information in the Requested WUS assistance information IE during attach or tracking area updating procedures when it is not attached for emergency bearer services. Specifically, it shall not include this information during an attach for emergency bearer services procedure or during a tracking area updating procedure when attached for emergency bearer services.
results.model_answer: A UE may include the UE paging probability IE in an ATTACH REQUEST or TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST when it supports WUS assistance and has a valid UE paging-probability value available. The IE is optional: its inclusion is not contingent on a particular attach type or TAU type, nor on prior network configuration of WUS; however, normal message applicability and UE capability signalling rules still apply.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2.2 (ATTACH REQUEST) and clause 5.5.3.2.2 (TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST). These procedure clauses specify that a UE supporting WUS assistance may include the UE paging probability IE when it has a valid UE paging probability.

results.question: How does a UE determine whether it is allowed to use WUS assistance after an attach or tracking area updating procedure?
results.reference: The UE shall use WUS assistance only if it received the Negotiated WUS assistance information IE during the last attach or tracking area updating procedure. If it did not receive this IE, it shall not use WUS assistance.
results.model_answer: The UE uses the network-provided WUS assistance indication/information in the successful ATTACH ACCEPT or TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT. It may use WUS assistance only when that received information explicitly permits it; if the indication/information is absent or does not permit use, the UE shall treat WUS assistance as not allowed. A later successful TAU can therefore enable, disable, or update the permission.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.13 (WUS assistance procedure), read with the UE handling of ATTACH ACCEPT and TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT and the WUS assistance information/indication IE definition. The normative rule is effectively that authorization is determined from the WUS assistance information received in the accept message, rather than inferred from UE capability or prior state.

results.question: What action must the network take regarding stored negotiated UE paging probability information if it does not accept a UE's request to use WUS assistance?
results.reference: If the network did not accept the request to use WUS assistance, it shall delete any stored negotiated UE paging probability information for that UE, if such information was available.
results.model_answer: The network shall delete any stored negotiated UE paging probability information when it does not accept the UE's request to use WUS assistance.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.11.3, UE assistance information procedure (WUS assistance handling): if the network does not accept the request to use WUS assistance, it shall delete any stored negotiated UE paging probability information.

results.question: Why might a UE be in the EMM-REGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE-MM state following a combined procedure?
results.reference: Because the combined attach or combined tracking area updating procedure was successful only for EPS services, not for non-EPS services, requiring the UE to continue attempting to update its mobility management context for the non-EPS service domain.
results.model_answer: A combined TA/LA update leaves the UE in EMM-REGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE-MM while the EPS mobility-management update is still being attempted. Typically, the UE sent a TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST with update type "combined TA/LA updating" and has not yet completed the transaction (for example, it is awaiting/processing a TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT, retransmitting after T3410 expiry, or retrying after a temporary failure). A successful TAU completion normally moves the UE to EMM-REGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE. Thus this state indicates an outstanding MM/TAU update attempt, not necessarily loss of EPS registration or a definitive CS-domain failure.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.2.3.2, "EMM-REGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE-MM state" (state is used while a tracking area updating/MM update is being attempted), together with clause 5.5.3, "Tracking area updating procedure", which defines combined TA/LA updating and its completion through TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT/REJECT handling.

results.question: How does the network's handling of user data and signalling relate to a UE entering the EMM-REGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE-MM state?
results.reference: The network permits the transmission and reception of user data and signalling information for the UE even while it is in this state, which is entered after a combined procedure succeeded for EPS services only.
results.model_answer: The state is a UE-side congestion/back-off state, not an indication that the network has accepted user-plane traffic. If the UE requests service (typically to send uplink user data or NAS signalling) and the network rejects that request with EMM cause #22 "congestion", the UE enters EMM-REGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE-MM (and applies the indicated/default T3346 back-off). Thus, the network's inability to accept the requested service/signalling is represented by the UE retaining EMM registration but deferring further normal service/signalling attempts until update/back-off handling permits recovery. It does not mean that the network has established user-plane resources; data requiring a new service request cannot be sent successfully while that request is rejected/backed off.
results.evidence: Most likely clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, §5.6.1.4 (SERVICE REJECT handling): on receipt of SERVICE REJECT with EMM cause #22 (congestion), the UE starts T3346 when applicable and enters EMM-REGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE-MM. Related cause semantics are in §9.9.3.9, EMM cause #22 "Congestion".

results.question: What specific procedural outcome triggers a transition to the EMM-REGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE-MM state?
results.reference: The successful completion of a combined attach procedure or a combined tracking area updating procedure, but where success is achieved solely for EPS services.
results.model_answer: The UE transitions to EMM-REGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE-MM when it initiates a tracking area updating (TAU) procedure.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.3 (Tracking area updating procedure): the UE enters EMM-REGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE-MM when the tracking area updating procedure is initiated.

results.question: How does the specification describe the implementation of the back-off timer in the UE?
results.reference: The back-off timer is described as a logical model of required UE behaviour and does not imply a specific implementation (e.g., as a timer or timestamp). The UE may use timer T3396 or different packet system specific timers as the back-off timer, which is a UE implementation decision.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.5.4.4.3, Handling of network rejection due to ESM cause other than ESM cause #26
results.model_answer: TS 24.301 defines the UE back-off mechanism as NAS timer T3346. It does not mandate an internal software implementation; it mandates the observable behavior. On a congestion-related reject, the UE starts T3346 using the network-supplied T3346 value IE (encoded as a GPRS Timer 3 value). If the congestion reject has no T3346 value IE, the specified default is 12 minutes. While T3346 is running, the UE applies the specified access/EMM-procedure restrictions and does not make normal re-attempts that would defeat the network-requested back-off; the timer expiry removes that restriction. Emergency and other explicitly specified exception procedures are not barred.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 11.2.2, "T3346 (back-off timer)". The associated UE actions are specified in the ATTACH REJECT, TRACKING AREA UPDATE REJECT, and SERVICE REJECT handling procedures (notably the reject handling text in clauses 5.5.1, 5.5.3, and 5.6.1, release dependent).

results.question: How can the network determine that a UE is using satellite E-UTRAN access and what action might be taken based on this determination?
results.reference: The MME can determine that a UE is accessing the network using a satellite E-UTRAN access, and based on this determination, it may enforce mobility restriction for the UE as specified in 3GPP TS 23.401.
results.model_answer: The MME can determine this from E-UTRAN-provided access information for the serving cell (i.e., a satellite-access indication/cell or TA configuration identifying the E-UTRAN access as satellite), rather than relying on the UE to infer it in NAS. The MME can then apply satellite-specific operator handling, for example access-policy/service restrictions or satellite-appropriate mobility and timer treatment. The specification permits such differentiated handling; it does not require one single mandatory action for every satellite-attached UE.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.3.2 (EPS attach procedure, MME processing of ATTACH REQUEST), together with the NAS general principle that the MME uses E-UTRAN/S1 access information, including serving-cell/TA information, when processing mobility-management procedures. The satellite-access status is an access-network fact supplied/derivable from E-UTRAN context, and can be used by the MME for policy and procedure handling.

results.question: What are the two modes in which satellite E-UTRAN access can be supported with CIoT EPS optimization?
results.reference: Satellite E-UTRAN access can be supported in WB-S1 mode or NB-S1 mode when combined with CIoT EPS optimization.
results.model_answer: Satellite E-UTRAN access with CIoT EPS optimization is supported in two modes: (1) control-plane CIoT EPS optimization, where small data is transported using NAS signalling via the MME; and (2) user-plane CIoT EPS optimization, where data is carried on the EPS user plane using the optimized user-plane procedures.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause titled "Support for satellite access" (within clause 4.3.5, Miscellaneous procedures; subclause numbering is release/version dependent). The clause states that satellite E-UTRAN access with CIoT EPS optimization can be supported using either control-plane CIoT EPS optimization or user-plane CIoT EPS optimization.

results.question: Where is the support for satellite E-UTRAN access formally specified within the 3GPP standards?
results.reference: Support for satellite E-UTRAN access is specified in 3GPP TS 36.300.
results.model_answer: Satellite E-UTRAN access is formally specified at EPS architecture/stage-2 level in 3GPP TS 23.401, in the clause titled "Support for satellite access" (commonly numbered clause 4.3.31 in recent releases; clause numbering should be checked against the applicable release). TS 24.301 is the EPS NAS stage-3 specification: it specifies the UE/MME NAS behaviour and messages used over E-UTRAN, but it is not the primary architectural specification that introduces satellite E-UTRAN access.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 23.401, clause "Support for satellite access": this is the normative EPS/EPC architecture clause defining support for satellite access via E-UTRAN. TS 24.301 applies the EPS NAS protocol to that access, subject to the procedures and capabilities defined for the relevant release.

results.question: How should a network entity handle a NAS message containing a syntactically incorrect optional information element?
results.reference: The network entity shall treat the syntactically incorrect optional IE as if it had not been received, ignoring its content while continuing to process the rest of the message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 7.7, Non-imperative message part errors
results.model_answer: The receiving network entity should ignore the syntactically incorrect optional information element and continue processing the remainder of the NAS message as if that optional IE were not present. It should not reject the whole message solely because an optional IE is syntactically incorrect, unless another procedure-specific rule applies.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.6 (Handling of unknown, unforeseen and erroneous protocol data), in the rules for syntactically incorrect information elements: a syntactically incorrect optional IE is ignored; message processing continues without use of that IE. The stricter invalid-mandatory-information handling applies to mandatory IEs, not optional IEs.

results.question: What distinguishes the handling of syntactically incorrect optional IEs from other types of message errors in NAS procedures?
results.reference: Syntactically incorrect optional IEs are specifically categorized as non-imperative errors, allowing the receiver to ignore them rather than rejecting the entire message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 7.7, Non-imperative message part errors
results.model_answer: A syntactically incorrect optional IE is handled locally: the receiver ignores that IE and continues processing the remainder of the NAS message. It is not, merely because that optional IE is malformed, treated as a message-level failure requiring message discard, a NAS STATUS response, or procedure rejection. This differs from errors involving mandatory information, unsupported/unknown mandatory content, semantic errors, or invalid message/state conditions, for which TS 24.301 defines message-error handling such as rejection, discard, or STATUS with an appropriate cause.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 8.2.7, "Syntactically incorrect optional IE": the receiver shall ignore the syntactically incorrect optional IE and continue to process the message. This is a specific exception to the more disruptive handling specified for other protocol/message errors in clause 8.2.

results.question: How does the specification address scenarios where a conditional IE is present but contains invalid content or structure?
results.reference: When a conditional information element (IE) is present but has invalid content or structure, the specification treats this as a non-imperative message part error. Such errors do not require rejecting the message as a whole; instead, the receiver applies defined error-handling rules, which may include ignoring the erroneous conditional IE or the entire message and, where applicable, returning a status message indicating a conditional IE error.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.501, Clause 7.7, Non-imperative message part errors
results.model_answer: A conditional IE is not simply ignored because it is optional/conditional. If it is present and is incorrectly coded (invalid value, length, format, or other content/structural error), TS 24.301 classifies this as a "conditional IE error" and uses cause value #100 where the applicable EMM/ESM procedure reports a cause. A conditionally mandatory IE that is required by the applicable condition but absent is handled by the same #100 category. The receiving entity follows the error-handling rule of the specific NAS procedure/message (for example, rejection or STATUS with the applicable cause); a malformed mandatory IE is instead normally associated with #96 "invalid mandatory information."
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.3 (EMM cause) and clause 9.9.4 (ESM cause): cause value #100, "Conditional IE error," covers a conditional IE error, including a conditionally mandatory IE missing when required or a conditional IE present but incorrectly coded. The message/procedure-specific error-handling clauses determine whether an EMM STATUS, ESM STATUS, reject, or other response is sent.

results.question: What is the purpose of the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT message according to the 3GPP specification?
results.reference: The message is sent by the UE to the network to reject the activation of a default EPS bearer context.
results.model_answer: The ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT message is sent by the UE to the network to refuse activation of a default EPS bearer context requested by the network. It conveys the UE's rejection and the applicable ESM cause.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 8.3.3 (ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT): "The ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT message is sent by the UE to the network to reject the activation of a default EPS bearer context."

results.question: Why are the procedures in clauses 7.1 to 7.8 applied in a specific order?
results.reference: The procedures are applied in a specific order to define a clear order of precedence for handling unknown, unforeseen, and erroneous protocol data, ensuring that critical error conditions are processed first while maintaining consistent error recovery and forward compatibility with future protocol extensions.
results.model_answer: They are not mandated to execute in the numerical order of clauses 7.1 through 7.8. The clause order is primarily document organization. Actual EMM procedure sequencing is selected by UE/MME triggers, the current EMM/ECM state, available EPS security context, and explicit procedure-collision rules. Where procedures are chained, the order preserves dependencies: identity may be obtained before authentication; authentication and NAS security-mode control establish a valid security context; attach or TAU establishes/updates registration and mobility context; service request uses an existing registered context; detach removes that context. Thus any apparent order reflects state, security, and context dependencies, not a general requirement to run clause 7 procedures sequentially.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 7.1 (General). It introduces the EMM-specific procedures that are subsequently specified; it does not impose a universal clause-number execution sequence. The normative ordering is instead found in each individual procedure's triggering conditions, state requirements, message flow, security requirements, and abnormal/procedure-collision handling (for example, the attach, TAU, service-request, authentication, identification, and security-mode-control clauses).

results.question: How does the network use the T3412 extended value IE to influence UE behavior?
results.reference: By including it in a message to assign a longer duration for the periodic tracking area update timer.
results.model_answer: The MME uses the optional T3412 extended value IE in ATTACH ACCEPT or TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT to provision the UE's extended periodic tracking-area-update timer (T3412). When present and supported, the UE uses this IE's GPRS Timer 3 value for T3412 rather than the legacy T3412 value IE. Thus, the network can lengthen, shorten, or deactivate periodic TAU behavior; expiry causes the UE to initiate periodic TAU. A long configured value supports long UE sleep/PSM intervals, but the IE does not itself configure active time (that is T3324).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clauses 5.5.1.2.4 (ATTACH ACCEPT handling) and 5.5.3.2.4 (TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT handling): on receipt of a T3412 extended value IE, the UE sets T3412 according to that IE; otherwise it uses the normal T3412 value IE. See also the TS 24.301 T3412 extended value IE definition, which specifies GPRS Timer 3 coding, including the deactivated value.

results.question: Under what condition might the network include the T3412 extended value IE?
results.reference: When it intends for the UE to use a longer timer interval for periodic tracking area updates.
results.model_answer: The network may include the T3412 extended value IE in an ATTACH ACCEPT or TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT when extended periodic TAU is supported by the network and the UE has indicated support for extended periodic timers in its UE network capability. It is used when the network elects to assign an extended T3412 periodic-TAU value (e.g., beyond the useful range of the legacy T3412 encoding).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1 (attach procedure) and clause 5.5.3 (tracking area updating procedure): the network's inclusion of the T3412 extended value IE is conditional on support for extended periodic TAU/extended periodic timers and UE indication of that capability. See also the ATTACH ACCEPT and TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message definitions in clause 9.4.

results.question: What two actions must the MME take upon receiving the SECURITY MODE COMPLETE message?
results.reference: The MME must stop timer T3460 and from that time onward, integrity protect and encipher all signalling messages using the selected NAS integrity and ciphering algorithms.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.3.4, NAS security mode control completion by the network
results.model_answer: The MME shall (1) stop timer T3460 and (2) consider the security mode control procedure successfully completed.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.4.3.2 (Security mode control procedure accepted by the UE): "Upon receipt of the SECURITY MODE COMPLETE message, the MME shall stop timer T3460 and shall consider that the security mode control procedure has been successfully completed."

results.question: How does the MME handle a SECURITY MODE COMPLETE message that contains a Replayed NAS container with an ATTACH REQUEST?
results.reference: The MME completes the ongoing attach procedure by considering the ATTACH REQUEST message within the Replayed NAS container as the message that triggered the procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.3.4, NAS security mode control completion by the network
results.model_answer: After successfully processing SECURITY MODE COMPLETE (including NAS integrity verification and activation/use of the selected NAS security context), the MME extracts the ATTACH REQUEST carried in the Replayed NAS message container and processes it according to the normal Attach Request handling procedure. The contained ATTACH REQUEST is treated as the replay of the NAS message that triggered security-mode control, not as a separate new attach transaction. If SECURITY MODE COMPLETE cannot be accepted (for example, NAS security verification fails), the contained request is not processed.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.4.3.3 (Security mode complete): on receipt of SECURITY MODE COMPLETE, the MME processes a message included in the Replayed NAS message container. Where that message is an ATTACH REQUEST, its processing is governed by clause 5.5.1.2 (Attach request).

results.question: What is the procedural consequence when the SECURITY MODE COMPLETE includes a Replayed NAS container with a TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST?
results.reference: The MME completes the ongoing tracking area updating procedure, treating the TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST inside the container as the original triggering message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.3.4, NAS security mode control completion by the network
results.model_answer: The MME shall process the replayed TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST and proceed with the tracking area updating procedure. The replayed request is the UE’s initial TAU request, now conveyed after successful NAS security-mode establishment; it is not treated as a new, separate TAU attempt.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.4.3 (security mode control procedure, MME-side handling of SECURITY MODE COMPLETE): when SECURITY MODE COMPLETE contains a Replayed NAS message container carrying a TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST, the MME proceeds with the tracking area updating procedure specified in clause 5.5.3.

results.question: From what point in time must the MME apply integrity protection and ciphering to all signalling messages?
results.reference: From the time the MME receives and processes the SECURITY MODE COMPLETE message, after stopping timer T3460.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.3.4, NAS security mode control completion by the network
results.model_answer: The MME must apply NAS integrity protection and ciphering to all subsequent NAS signalling messages after successful completion of the security mode control procedure (i.e., once the new NAS security context has been activated).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.4.3 (Security mode control procedure): following successful completion of the procedure, the MME applies integrity protection and ciphering to NAS signalling messages sent to the UE.

results.question: What is the primary purpose of the network sending an EMM INFORMATION message to the UE?
results.reference: To provide information from the network to the UE.
results.model_answer: The primary purpose is to provide the UE with network-provided informational parameters: the operator/network name and time-related information (universal time, local time zone, and daylight-saving time). It is an informational downlink NAS procedure, not an authentication, registration, or mobility-control procedure.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.3.1 (EMM information procedure — General): "The purpose of the EMM information procedure is to provide the UE with the network name, universal time and local time zone, and daylight saving time."

results.question: How is the implementation of the EMM INFORMATION message characterized for the network?
results.reference: It is optional for the network to implement.
results.model_answer: For the network, the EMM INFORMATION procedure/message is optional to implement. If implemented, it is a network-initiated downlink procedure used to provide access-network information to an EMM-REGISTERED UE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1 (EMM information procedure — General): the EMM information procedure is specified as optional to implement for the network and the UE.

results.question: Under what condition can a UE utilize the information received in an EMM INFORMATION message?
results.reference: If the UE supports implementing this message.
results.model_answer: A UE may utilize information in an EMM INFORMATION message only when the message is received while the UE is in EMM-REGISTERED state. Information received while in EMM-DEREGISTERED state shall not be used.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.2.2 (UE behaviour for the EMM information procedure): the UE shall only use information received in an EMM INFORMATION message if the message is received in EMM-REGISTERED state.

results.question: What is the purpose of the Paging identity information element as defined in the clause?
results.reference: The purpose is to indicate the identity used for paging for non-EPS services.
results.model_answer: The Paging identity IE identifies the UE for which the NAS PAGING message is intended, enabling the addressed UE to recognize that it is being paged and to perform the applicable follow-on NAS action.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.3.30 (Paging identity): the clause defines the IE as the identity used to identify the UE to be paged.

results.question: According to the clause, which resources specify the coding of the Paging identity information element?
results.reference: The coding is specified in figure 9.9.3.25A.1 and table 9.9.3.25A.1.
results.model_answer: The Paging identity IE coding is specified by 3GPP TS 24.008, subclause 10.5.1.4 (Mobile identity), which defines the encoding for identities such as IMSI and TMSI/S-TMSI.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, Paging identity IE clause: “The coding of the Paging identity information element is specified in 3GPP TS 24.008 [13], subclause 10.5.1.4.”

results.question: How does the UE handle the CSFB response IE for a mobile terminating 1xCS fallback scenario?
results.reference: The UE does not include the CSFB response IE for mobile terminating 1xCS fallback, as explicitly noted.
results.model_answer: For a mobile-terminating 1xCS fallback page, the UE sends an EXTENDED SERVICE REQUEST with Service type set to "mobile terminating CS fallback". The UE includes the CSFB response IE and sets it to "CS fallback accepted by the UE" when it accepts the requested 1xCS fallback. This IE is UE-to-network feedback; it informs the MME whether the UE accepts or rejects CS fallback, rather than being a response received from the network.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.6.1.1 (initiation of the extended service request procedure): for an MT 1xCS fallback indication/page, the UE initiates the extended service request procedure, uses the mobile-terminating CS-fallback service type, and includes the CSFB response IE with the acceptance indication. The CSFB response IE coding/semantics are specified in clause 9.9.3 (CSFB response IE).

results.question: Explain the relationship between the Service type IE and the CSFB response IE inclusion.
results.reference: The UE's inclusion of the CSFB response IE is conditional upon the Service type IE indicating "mobile terminating CS fallback or 1xCS fallback", with an exception that it is not included for mobile terminating 1xCS fallback.
results.model_answer: In an EXTENDED SERVICE REQUEST, the Service type IE controls whether the CSFB response IE is conditionally mandatory. The UE includes the CSFB response IE when Service type indicates "mobile terminating CS fallback" or "mobile terminating CS fallback and 1xCS fallback". The CSFB response then reports whether the UE accepts CS fallback. For signalling, data, mobile-originated CS fallback, and other Service type values, this IE is not required by that condition.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 8.2.12, EXTENDED SERVICE REQUEST message-content table. The presence condition on the "CSFB response" IE states that it shall be included when the Service type IE is set to "mobile terminating CS fallback" or "mobile terminating CS fallback and 1xCS fallback". The CSFB response IE encoding itself is specified in clause 9.9.2.1.

results.question: Why does a network need to reference 3GPP TS 36.331 when supporting offloading of traffic to WLAN?
results.reference: Because the offloading of traffic to WLAN is specified in 3GPP TS 36.331, which defines the relevant mechanisms for the network.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.3.7, Handling of WLAN offload control
results.model_answer: TS 24.301 does not define the radio-interface encoding or delivery of WLAN-offload assistance. When E-UTRAN wants a UE to consider WLAN for offload, it must provide the WLAN-offload information using the RRC mechanisms defined by TS 36.331 (notably broadcast system information). Therefore the network/eNB must reference TS 36.331 to know the applicable RRC information element, its encoding, broadcast scheduling and UE processing. This is offload assistance/selection information; it is not a NAS procedure for moving the user-plane packets themselves to WLAN.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, the clause titled "WLAN offload" (clause numbering is release-dependent), which directs WLAN-offload support/UE use of WLAN-offload information to TS 36.331. The corresponding technical definition is in TS 36.331 clause 6.2.2, SystemInformationBlockType17 (SIB17), including WLAN-OffloadInfo.

results.question: How does the handling of WLAN offload control relate to the UE and the PDN connection in a supporting network?
results.reference: A permission to offload traffic to WLAN is determined specifically for both the UE and the PDN connection, following the standards referenced in the clause.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.3.7, Handling of WLAN offload control
results.model_answer: In a network that supports WLAN offload control, WLAN offload permission is controlled per PDN connection, not as a blanket UE-wide permission. The UE shall only offload traffic for a particular PDN connection to WLAN when the network has indicated that WLAN offload is allowed for that PDN connection. The UE retains/uses the received WLAN offload indication in the context of the corresponding PDN connection; absence of permission is treated conservatively, i.e. the UE must not offload that PDN connection merely on its own decision.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.10.2 (PDN connectivity procedure), WLAN offload-control behaviour. The normative rule is that, when registered in a network supporting WLAN offload control, the UE shall not perform WLAN offload for a PDN connection unless it has received a network indication that WLAN offload is allowed for that PDN connection.

results.question: Under what conditions is the N1 UE network capability IE required to be included by the UE?
results.reference: The UE must include the IE if it supports N1 mode and needs to indicate its supported CIoT network behaviour for the 5G Core Network.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 9.9.3.57, N1 UE network capability
results.model_answer: The UE shall include the N1 UE network capability IE when it supports N1 mode. This requirement applies when the UE sends an EPS ATTACH REQUEST or a TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST; the IE is not required merely because the UE supports other 5GS/EPS interworking features if it does not support N1 mode.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.3 (N1 UE network capability IE): the IE shall be included by the UE in ATTACH REQUEST and TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST messages if the UE supports N1 mode. The ATTACH REQUEST and TAU REQUEST procedure text/message definitions are in clauses 5.5.1.2.2 and 5.5.3.2, respectively.

results.question: For what purpose does the UE include the N1 UE network capability IE?
results.reference: The UE includes it to indicate the supported CIoT network behaviour for the 5G Core Network when operating in N1 mode.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.4.24, N1 UE network capability
results.model_answer: The UE includes the N1 UE network capability IE to inform the EPS NAS network (MME) of its capabilities for N1 mode/5GS NAS operation. This enables the network to retain and use the UE's 5GS-related NAS capability information, including for EPS–5GS interworking and subsequent mobility toward 5GS.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.3, "N1 UE network capability" IE; the IE is defined as conveying the UE's N1-mode network capabilities. Related UE procedures require its inclusion in EPS registration/mobility-management requests when the UE supports N1 mode.

results.question: How can the UE mode of operation change for a CS voice capable UE according to the specified clause?
results.reference: The UE mode of operation for a CS voice capable UE can change due to: a change of the UE's usage setting; a change of voice domain preference for E-UTRAN as defined in 3GPP TS 24.167; a change in the UE's availability for voice calls in the IMS; or a change in UE configuration regarding the use of SMS as defined in 3GPP TS 24.167.
results.model_answer: For a CS-voice-capable UE, the operational behaviour can change when the UE changes its UE usage setting and/or voice-domain preference for E-UTRAN (for example, voice-centric versus data-centric, or CS voice preferred/only versus IMS PS voice preferred/only). The change is UE-controlled, typically due to user or local configuration, and is reported to the network in the relevant NAS registration/update signalling (e.g., Attach or Tracking Area Update). The network may accept, reject, or constrain the resulting registration/service combination, but does not itself silently change the UE's configured preference.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 4.3.5, "UE's usage setting and voice domain preference for E-UTRAN". This clause defines that these parameters apply to CS-voice-capable UEs and govern whether the UE operates with a voice-centric/data-centric usage setting and a CS-voice or IMS-PS-voice preference; their changed values are conveyed in NAS mobility-management procedures.

results.question: After transitioning to PS mode 1 or PS mode 2 due to "CS domain not available", how can the UE transition back to CS/PS mode 1 or CS/PS mode 2?
results.reference: After such a transition, the UE can transition back to CS/PS mode 1 or CS/PS mode 2, for example, due to a change of PLMN which is not in the list of the equivalent PLMNs.
results.model_answer: The UE returns only as part of a successful combined registration/update outcome: it performs (or is performing) a combined attach or combined TAU procedure and receives an ATTACH ACCEPT or TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT that does not indicate EMM cause #39, "CS domain not available". It then enters the corresponding CS/PS mode (CS/PS mode 1 or CS/PS mode 2, according to the applicable IMSI-attach/CS-registration status). Mere detection that CS service may be available, or expiry of a timer, does not by itself change PS mode 1/2 back to CS/PS mode 1/2.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 4.3.5, UE mode of operation (CS/PS mode 1, CS/PS mode 2, PS mode 1 and PS mode 2). This clause specifies the mode change on receipt of ATTACH ACCEPT or TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT with EMM cause #39 "CS domain not available", and the return to a CS/PS mode when the relevant accept does not contain that cause. Relevant procedural support is in the attach and tracking-area-update procedures (TS 24.301 clause 5.5.1 and clause 5.5.3).

results.question: Under what condition is the UE required to include the Device properties IE in a NAS message according to clause 8.3.8.3?
results.reference: The UE is required to include the Device properties IE when it is configured for NAS signalling low priority.
results.model_answer: The UE is required to include the Device properties IE when it is configured for low-priority service (i.e., low-priority access) as specified by 3GPP TS 23.221.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 8.3.8.3 (Device properties): the UE shall include the Device properties IE in the relevant NAS request message when the UE is configured for low-priority service.

results.question: What configuration of the UE triggers the mandatory inclusion of the Device properties IE as specified?
results.reference: The mandatory inclusion is triggered when the UE is configured for NAS signalling low priority.
results.model_answer: Mandatory inclusion is triggered when the UE is configured for low priority. In that case, the UE shall include the Device properties IE, carrying the low-priority indication, in the applicable NAS request message.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2.2 (UE initiated attach procedure): the UE shall include the Device properties IE in the ATTACH REQUEST if the UE is configured for low priority. The corresponding conditional-presence rules also apply in relevant mobility/service request message specifications.

results.question: How does the UE determine whether to include the Device properties IE in its NAS signalling?
results.reference: The UE determines inclusion based on whether it is configured for NAS signalling low priority; if so, it shall include the IE.
results.model_answer: The UE makes this decision from its local low-priority configuration, not from a per-message network request. When the UE is configured for NAS signalling low priority, it includes the Device properties IE (with the low-priority indication set) in NAS messages whose procedure/message definition permits and requires that IE, notably normal ATTACH REQUEST and TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST procedures. If it is not configured for low priority, it does not include the IE merely to report a zero value. The message-specific rules still apply; in particular, the IE is not included for an emergency attach.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2 (ATTACH REQUEST message content/procedure): the UE shall include the Device properties IE when it is configured for low priority; the emergency-attach handling excludes this indication. Corresponding TAU behaviour is specified in clause 5.5.3.2.

results.question: What is the specific UE configuration that necessitates the presence of the Device properties IE?
results.reference: The specific configuration is the UE being set up for NAS signalling low priority.
results.model_answer: The UE shall include the Device properties IE when it is configured for NAS signalling low priority.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2.2 (ATTACH REQUEST message content): "The UE shall include the Device properties IE if the UE is configured for NAS signalling low priority" (with the low-priority configuration referenced to TS 23.401).

results.question: Why does a UE acting as a ProSe UE-to-network relay include the ProSe Key Management Function Address IE in a message?
results.reference: To provide the network with the address of the ProSe Key Management Function that is associated with the remote UEs connected to or disconnected from the relay.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.23.4, ProSe Key Management Function Address
results.model_answer: The relay UE includes the ProSe Key Management Function (PKMF) Address IE to identify the PKMF associated with its ProSe UE-to-network relay operation. This gives the EPS network/MME the PKMF endpoint needed to support the relay-related ProSe security and key-management procedures. The IE is therefore an identifier for network-side PKMF selection/contact; it is not itself ProSe key material or proof of relay authorization.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2 (UE-initiated attach procedure), in the requirements for a UE configured as a ProSe UE-to-network relay to include relay-related information, including the ProSe Key Management Function Address IE, in the ATTACH REQUEST. Related mobility-update requirements are in clause 5.5.3.2 (UE-initiated tracking area updating procedure). The IE definition is in TS 24.301 clause 9.9.3 (ProSe Key Management Function Address IE).

results.question: How does the network learn the address of the ProSe Key Management Function for remote UEs using a relay?
results.reference: The UE acting as a ProSe UE-to-network relay includes the ProSe Key Management Function Address IE in a message sent to the network.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.23.4, ProSe Key Management Function Address
results.model_answer: The network learns it from the relay UE. When a remote UE is served through a ProSe UE-to-Network Relay, the relay reports the remote UE to the network using the NAS Remote UE reporting procedure. The report carries the remote-UE-related information, including the ProSe Key Management Function (PKMF) address received/associated for that remote UE. Thus, the MME obtains the PKMF address from the relay's REMOTE UE REPORT; it is not derived from the relay UE's own PKMF address or subscription.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.13.4 (ProSe UE-to-Network Relay procedures), in the Remote UE reporting behavior for a relay UE; see also the NAS IE definition for the ProSe Key Management Function address in clause 9.9.3.

results.question: What specific role must a UE fulfill to include the ProSe Key Management Function Address IE, and what is the purpose?
results.reference: The UE must be acting as a ProSe UE-to-network relay, and the purpose is to inform the network of the ProSe Key Management Function address linked to remote UEs that are connecting to or disconnecting from this relay.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.23.4, ProSe Key Management Function Address
results.model_answer: The UE must be acting as a ProSe UE-to-Network Relay. It includes the ProSe Key Management Function (PKMF) Address IE to identify the PKMF associated with the relay service, enabling the network/relay security procedures to obtain or manage the ProSe security material needed for the relay operation.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.5.1.2 (PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message content and IE-presence conditions). The conditional rule for the ProSe Key Management Function Address IE associates its inclusion with a UE acting as a ProSe UE-to-Network Relay. The IE definition is in TS 24.301 clause 9.9.4 (ProSe Key Management Function Address IE).

results.question: Under what condition does the network initiate the paging procedure for CS fallback, and what is a key restriction on this initiation?
results.reference: The network may initiate paging for CS fallback when the UE is IMSI attached for non-EPS services. However, it should not initiate paging if the MME has stored paging restriction for the UE and the restriction type is set to 'All paging is restricted' or 'All paging is restricted except for specified PDN connection(s)'.
results.model_answer: The network initiates CS-fallback paging when a mobile-terminating CS service (for example, a CS call) is pending for a UE that is in EMM-IDLE and is eligible/registered for CS service via CS fallback. A key restriction is that this paging mechanism is for an idle UE: it must not be used to trigger CS fallback for a UE already in EMM-CONNECTED; the network uses the CS SERVICE NOTIFICATION procedure for that case.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.6.1 (paging procedure) specifies paging for a UE in EMM-IDLE, including paging with the CS domain indication for CS fallback. Clause 5.6.4 (CS service notification) covers notification of CS service when the UE is in EMM-CONNECTED, distinguishing that case from paging.

results.question: How does the network's EMM entity handle the provision of CSG ID lists to the lower layer during paging initiation for CS fallback, and what specific condition alters this handling?
results.reference: The EMM entity may provide the lower layer with a list of CSG IDs, including both expired and not expired subscriptions. However, if a PDN connection for emergency bearer services is established, the EMM entity shall not provide the list of CSG IDs to the lower layer.
results.model_answer: For CS-fallback paging, the network EMM entity passes the UE's CSG ID list to the lower layers so that paging can be performed consistently with CSG access restrictions. This is conditional: the list is passed only when it is available/has been stored for the UE; if no CSG ID list is available, the EMM entity does not provide such a list to the lower layers.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.3.4.3 (network-initiated service request/paging): when initiating paging for CS fallback, the EMM entity provides the CSG ID list, if available, to the lower layers. The qualifying condition "if available" is the condition that changes the handling.

results.question: What are the two primary methods by which the network notifies a UE about an incoming mobile terminating CS service (excluding SMS over SGs), and how do they differ based on the UE's connection state?
results.reference: When no NAS signalling connection exists and no paging restriction applies, the network initiates paging via the lower layer with a paging message containing a UE Paging Identity and CN domain indicator set to 'CS'. When a NAS signalling connection exists, the network sends a CS SERVICE NOTIFICATION message, which may include CS service related parameters.
results.model_answer: For an incoming mobile-terminating CS service (other than SMS over SGs), the network uses: (1) the CS service notification procedure when the UE is ECM-CONNECTED, by sending a NAS CS SERVICE NOTIFICATION message; and (2) the paging procedure when the UE is ECM-IDLE, by paging the UE with the CN-domain indication set to CS. Paging first re-establishes NAS/RRC connectivity; the UE then performs the appropriate extended service-request/CS-fallback handling. Thus, CS SERVICE NOTIFICATION is the direct notification method for an already connected UE, whereas paging is the reachability mechanism for an idle UE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.6.1 (CS service notification procedure — General): the CS service notification procedure is used to notify a UE of an incoming MT CS service when the UE is in ECM-CONNECTED; for a UE in ECM-IDLE, the network uses the paging procedure specified in 3GPP TS 23.401.

results.question: Under what specific condition related to handover should the MME retransmit an undelivered EMM INFORMATION message upon successful completion of an intra MME handover?
results.reference: The MME shall retransmit the EMM INFORMATION message upon successful completion of the intra MME handover only if the target TA (Tracking Area) is included in the TAI (Tracking Area Identity) list.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.5.4, Abnormal cases on the network side
results.model_answer: The MME shall retransmit the EMM INFORMATION message only when the intra-MME handover has completed successfully and the message had not been delivered to the UE by the source eNodeB before the handover. The retransmission is sent via the target eNodeB.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2 (initiation of the EMM information procedure): the MME retransmits an EMM INFORMATION message not delivered before a successfully completed intra-MME handover.

results.question: How does the network utilize the Extended EMM cause IE in relation to a primary EMM cause?
results.reference: It is included to supplement the primary EMM cause with further explanatory details.
results.model_answer: The network uses the Extended EMM cause IE only as a qualifier to the primary EMM cause IE: it supplies additional, more specific information associated with the EMM cause conveyed in the NAS reject message. It does not replace the primary EMM cause; the EMM cause remains the principal rejection reason, while the extended cause refines that reason when applicable.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.3.9A (Extended EMM cause): the IE is defined for providing additional information associated with the EMM cause IE. The corresponding primary cause is defined in clause 9.9.3.9 (EMM cause).

results.question: What role does the Extended EMM cause IE serve in the context of EMM cause signaling?
results.reference: It acts as an optional carrier for supplementary details related to the reason for an EMM procedure outcome.
results.model_answer: The Extended EMM cause IE supplements the normal EMM cause indication with a more specific, extended cause value when the legacy EMM-cause field alone cannot express the applicable reason. It preserves interoperability: a UE can act on the ordinary EMM cause, while a UE supporting the extended IE can use the additional standardized diagnostic/behavioural information. Its presence is message- and procedure-dependent, as specified by the relevant EMM message table.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause "Extended EMM cause" in section 9.9.3 (information elements), which defines the IE as carrying an extended EMM-cause indication; the EMM message definitions specify when that optional IE may accompany the regular EMM cause.

results.question: How should the UE respond if, during an ongoing attach or tracking area updating procedure, the HASHMME in the SECURITY MODE COMMAND message differs from the locally calculated hash value?
results.reference: If HASHMME and the locally calculated hash value are different, the UE must include the complete ATTACH REQUEST or TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message that it had previously sent in the Replayed NAS message container IE of the SECURITY MODE COMPLETE message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.3.3, NAS security mode command accepted by the UE
results.model_answer: The UE shall abort the ongoing attach or tracking area updating procedure and enter EMM-DEREGISTERED state if the HASHMME received in the SECURITY MODE COMMAND does not match the UE's locally calculated HASHMME. It does not proceed with security-mode completion for that procedure.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.4.3.2 (SECURITY MODE COMMAND message reception): when the HASHMME IE is included, the UE calculates HASHMME and compares it with the received value; on mismatch, the UE shall abort the ongoing attach or tracking area updating procedure and enter EMM-DEREGISTERED state.

results.question: Under what condition is the EMM-REGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE substate chosen by the UE?
results.reference: This substate is chosen when the UE enters the EMM-REGISTERED state, serving as the primary substate for that entry.
results.model_answer: The UE selects EMM-REGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE when its EPS update status is EU1 UPDATED and it is camped on a suitable cell. In practical terms, this is the registered, normally serviceable condition—typically reached after successful attach or tracking area updating, provided no cell/PLMN/TA restriction requires another EMM-REGISTERED substate.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.3.2.1 (EMM-REGISTERED substates): the UE enters/selects EMM-REGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE when the EPS update status is EU1 UPDATED and the UE is camping on a suitable cell.

results.question: What role does the EMM-REGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE substate play in the UE's state management?
results.reference: It functions as the primary substate that the UE selects upon transitioning into the EMM-REGISTERED state.
results.model_answer: EMM-REGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE is the UE's stable EMM registered substate for normal EPS operation. It indicates that the UE has a valid EPS registration and is permitted normal service; it is therefore the baseline from which the UE handles ordinary mobility and service events, such as responding to paging, initiating a Service Request when needed, and initiating tracking area updating when an update trigger arises. It is an EMM/NAS registration-and-service condition, independent of whether the UE is currently ECM-IDLE or ECM-CONNECTED.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.1.3.3, "EMM-REGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE" (most likely evidence clause). This clause defines the registered normal-service substate; the associated state-transition and procedure clauses specify entry following successful registration/update handling and transitions when update, PLMN search, limited service, or loss-of-cell conditions apply.

results.question: How does the mobile station classmark 3 information element relate to the specifications in 3GPP TS 24.008?
results.reference: The content and definition of the mobile station classmark 3 information element are not provided directly in TS 24.301; instead, the clause explicitly references and defers to clause 10.5.1.7 in 3GPP TS 24.008 for its complete specification.
results.model_answer: TS 24.301 does not define an independent LTE-specific coding for the Mobile station classmark 3 IE. It normatively reuses the IE specified by TS 24.008: its format, length/coding and capability-bit interpretation are defined in TS 24.008 subclause 10.5.1.7. TS 24.301 only determines when the IE may or shall be carried in an EPS NAS message. Thus, it conveys legacy GERAN/CS-domain MS classmark capabilities, not UE radio capability information newly defined for E-UTRAN.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.3 "Mobile station classmark 3": "The Mobile station classmark 3 information element is specified in 3GPP TS 24.008 ... subclause 10.5.1.7." The referenced TS 24.008 clause is "Mobile station classmark 3".

results.question: Why would a developer need to consult 3GPP TS 24.008 when implementing the mobile station classmark 3 as per TS 24.301?
results.reference: Because TS 24.301 clause 9.9.2.5 does not contain the technical details or structure of the mobile station classmark 3; it solely points to an external clause in a different specification (TS 24.008) for the authoritative definition.
results.model_answer: TS 24.301 defines the EPS NAS usage of the MS classmark 3 IE (e.g., message placement/presence), but delegates its actual IE coding to TS 24.008. A developer therefore must consult TS 24.008 to encode and decode the classmark-3 length and bit fields correctly, including capability bits and extension/variable-length handling. Implementing from TS 24.301 alone risks interoperable-format errors for GERAN/CS-fallback and inter-RAT capability signalling.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.3, "MS classmark 3", states that the MS classmark 3 information element is coded as specified in 3GPP TS 24.008. The corresponding detailed coding definition is in 3GPP TS 24.008, clause 10.5.1.7, "Mobile station classmark 3".

results.question: What is the purpose of the cross-reference to TS 24.008 in the specification for mobile station classmark 3?
results.reference: The cross-reference serves to avoid duplication of technical details, directing the reader to the primary source document (TS 24.008) where the complete and formal definition of the mobile station classmark 3 information element is maintained.
results.model_answer: The cross-reference normatively incorporates the TS 24.008 definition of the Mobile station classmark 3 IE into TS 24.301. Thus, TS 24.301 specifies where the IE may be carried in EPS NAS procedures, while TS 24.008 supplies its IE format, coding and capability semantics. This preserves a common GSM/UMTS classmark representation for inter-RAT/legacy capability information; it does not create a separate LTE-specific classmark-3 encoding.
results.evidence: TS 24.301, clause 9.9.3.17 (Mobile station classmark 3), states in substance: "The Mobile station classmark 3 IE is defined in 3GPP TS 24.008 [13]." The referenced definition is TS 24.008, clause 10.5.1.5, Mobile Station Classmark 3.

results.question: How is the mobile station classmark 3 information element defined within the structure of TS 24.301?
results.reference: It is not defined within TS 24.301's own text; the clause acts as a pointer, indicating that the definitive specification is located entirely in another document, specifically clause 10.5.1.7 of TS 24.008.
results.model_answer: TS 24.301 does not define an independent bit-level format for the Mobile station classmark 3 IE. In its IE definitions, it incorporates the IE by reference: it shall be coded as the Mobile station classmark 3 IE specified in TS 24.008, clause 10.5.1.7. Thus, TS 24.301 uses the 24.008 classmark-3 syntax/content, rather than redefining it for EPS NAS.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.3.21, "Mobile station classmark 3": "The Mobile station classmark 3 information element is coded as the Mobile station classmark 3 information element specified in 3GPP TS 24.008 ... subclause 10.5.1.7."

results.question: How many bits are allocated for the Security header type IE in the first octet of an EMM message, and what is its total size?
results.reference: Bits 5 to 8 of the first octet are allocated for the Security header type IE, and its total size is 4 bits.
results.model_answer: The Security header type occupies 4 bits (one half-octet) in the first octet of an EMM message. Its IE size is therefore 4 bits; it shares octet 1 with the 4-bit EPS mobility management protocol discriminator.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.3.1 (Security header type): the Security header type is a type 1 information element with length 4 bits. In the EMM message header, it is carried in bits 5 to 8 of octet 1, while bits 1 to 4 carry the EPS mobility management protocol discriminator.

results.question: What should a protocol entity do when sending a not security protected EMM message regarding the security header type encoding?
results.reference: It shall send the message as a plain NAS message and encode the security header type as 0000.
results.model_answer: When sending an EMM message without NAS security protection, the protocol entity shall encode the 4-bit Security Header Type as "0000" (plain NAS message). It shall therefore use the plain EMM NAS header, without the security-protected-header MAC and sequence-number fields.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 4.4.3 (Security header type), in particular the Security header type encoding for EMM messages: value "0000" denotes a plain NAS message that is not security protected. The normative sending rule is that a not security protected EMM message is sent with Security Header Type set to "0000".

results.question: How should an EMM message be treated if it is received with the security header type encoded as 0000?
results.reference: It shall be treated as a not security protected, plain NAS message.
results.model_answer: Treat it as a plain, unprotected NAS/EMM message: it has neither NAS integrity protection nor NAS ciphering. Therefore, do not perform MAC verification or deciphering based on the NAS security header; process it only where the applicable EMM procedure permits reception of an unprotected message, otherwise reject/discard it according to that procedure's security requirements.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 4.4.3.1 (NAS security header / Security header type). Security header type value 0000 denotes a "Plain NAS message, not security protected."

results.question: For what specific message type is the codepoint referenced in NOTE 2 exclusively permitted?
results.reference: The codepoint may be used only for a SECURITY MODE COMPLETE message.
results.model_answer: The codepoint is exclusively permitted for the SERVICE REQUEST message.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.3.1 (Security header type), NOTE 2: security header type codepoint "1100" is only applicable to the SERVICE REQUEST message.

results.question: Under what two conditions must the Extended APN aggregate maximum bit rate IE be included in a message according to the clause?
results.reference: The IE must be included only if the network wants to send APN-AMBR values to the UE for potential uplink policy enforcement, and at least one of those values exceeds the maximum limit defined in the APN aggregate maximum bit rate IE in clause 9.9.4.2.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.6.17, Extended APN aggregate maximum bit rate
results.model_answer: The Extended APN aggregate maximum bit rate IE shall be included when either APN-AMBR direction exceeds 256 Mbps: (1) downlink APN-AMBR > 256 Mbps, or (2) uplink APN-AMBR > 256 Mbps. Either condition is sufficient; both are not required.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.4.2 (Extended APN aggregate maximum bit rate): the IE shall be included when the APN aggregate maximum bit rate exceeds 256 Mbps in the downlink and/or uplink direction.

results.question: How does the value of the APN-AMBR relate to the necessity of including the Extended APN aggregate maximum bit rate IE?
results.reference: The Extended APN aggregate maximum bit rate IE is required only when at least one APN-AMBR value to be transmitted is greater than the maximum value specified in the standard APN aggregate maximum bit rate information element.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.6.17, Extended APN aggregate maximum bit rate
results.model_answer: The Extended APN aggregate maximum bit rate IE is conditionally required when the APN-AMBR exceeds the range representable by the ordinary APN-AMBR IE, i.e. when the APN-AMBR is greater than 256 Mbps in the uplink and/or downlink direction. At or below 256 Mbps, the ordinary APN-AMBR IE is sufficient and the Extended IE is not required.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, the conditional-presence rule for the "Extended APN aggregate maximum bit rate" IE in applicable ESM message-content tables: "This IE shall be included if the APN-AMBR is greater than 256 Mbps." The ordinary APN-AMBR IE encoding represents rates up to 256 Mbps; the Extended IE carries the higher-rate representation.

results.question: What determines whether the network should include the Extended APN aggregate maximum bit rate IE instead of relying on the regular APN aggregate maximum bit rate IE?
results.reference: The network should include the Extended IE when it needs to convey APN-AMBR values that exceed the capacity of the regular APN aggregate maximum bit rate IE defined in clause 9.9.4.2.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.6.17, Extended APN aggregate maximum bit rate
results.model_answer: The trigger is the negotiated APN-AMBR value together with UE capability. If the APN aggregate maximum bit rate cannot be adequately encoded by the legacy APN aggregate maximum bit rate IE, the network uses the Extended APN aggregate maximum bit rate IE, provided that the UE has indicated support for extended APN-AMBR. The extended IE is therefore not selected by APN identity or bearer type; it is needed for an AMBR outside the regular IE's coding range. In practice it supplements the regular IE for compatibility rather than being an unconditional replacement for it.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.4.1 (PDN connectivity procedure / PDN CONNECTIVITY ACCEPT message-content requirements), read with the APN aggregate maximum bit rate and Extended APN aggregate maximum bit rate IE definitions in clause 9.9.4: the network's inclusion of the extended IE is conditional on the UE's extended-APN-AMBR capability and is used when the APN-AMBR requires the extended encoding.

results.question: How can a UE with active PSM initiate mobile originated signalling or user data transmission while in the EMM-REGISTERED.NO-CELL-AVAILABLE state?
results.reference: The UE can deactivate PSM by activating the Access Stratum (AS) layer when it needs to send mobile originated signalling or user data.
results.model_answer: It cannot transmit NAS signalling or user data while no suitable/acceptable cell is available. A pending MO signalling/data request causes the UE to leave PSM (if it is in PSM) and perform/resume PLMN and cell selection. After finding and camping on a suitable cell, it moves to EMM-REGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE and can initiate the applicable access procedure (normally Service Request; Control Plane Service Request for CIoT CP optimisation). If a TAU is required before service, the UE performs TAU first. Until a cell is found, the UE defers/buffers the MO request; PSM does not provide an alternative transmission path in EMM-REGISTERED.NO-CELL-AVAILABLE. Emergency access is a separate exceptional case.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.1.2.2.2 (EMM-REGISTERED state and its substates), specifically EMM-REGISTERED.NO-CELL-AVAILABLE: this substate applies when the UE cannot find a suitable/acceptable cell and requires cell selection before normal service can be obtained. Supporting clause: TS 24.301, clause 5.4.5 (Power Saving Mode), which specifies leaving PSM for UE-originated activity; leaving PSM does not remove the need to obtain a cell. Service Request behaviour is specified in TS 24.301 clause 5.3.4.

results.question: What EMM procedures is a UE prohibited from initiating in the EMM-REGISTERED.NO-CELL-AVAILABLE state when neither coverage loss nor PSM deactivation applies?
results.reference: The UE shall not initiate any EMM procedures except for cell reselection and PLMN reselection.
results.model_answer: The UE is prohibited from initiating any EMM procedure in EMM-REGISTERED.NO-CELL-AVAILABLE. Thus, absent the stated coverage-loss or PSM-deactivation exceptions, it must not initiate procedures such as TAU, Service Request, Attach, or Detach.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.1.3.3.6, "EMM-REGISTERED.NO-CELL-AVAILABLE state" (clause numbering can vary by release). The normative rule states that, except for EMM procedures initiated due to coverage loss or deactivation of PSM, the UE shall not initiate any EMM procedure in this state.

results.question: Under what specific condition is a UE allowed to perform an exception to the general prohibition on initiating EMM procedures in the EMM-REGISTERED.NO-CELL-AVAILABLE state?
results.reference: The UE is allowed to perform cell reselection and PLMN reselection procedures, which are the only EMM procedures it can initiate in this state.
results.model_answer: A UE in EMM-REGISTERED.NO-CELL-AVAILABLE may make the exception only to initiate a UE-initiated detach procedure when the UE is being switched off.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.2.2.2.2.4 (EMM-REGISTERED.NO-CELL-AVAILABLE): the UE shall not initiate any EMM procedure in this state, except for the detach procedure when the UE is switched off.

results.question: Under what specific condition is the UE required to include the replayed NAS message container information element?
results.reference: The UE must include it if, during an ongoing attach or tracking area updating procedure, the MME included HASHMME in the SECURITY MODE COMMAND message and that HASHMME value differs from the hash value the UE calculated locally.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.21.3, Replayed NAS message container
results.model_answer: The UE shall include the Replayed NAS message container IE in the SECURITY MODE COMPLETE message when the received SECURITY MODE COMMAND contains a NAS message container IE. The UE replays the NAS message conveyed by that container; security-mode-control execution alone does not trigger this IE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.4.3.3 (security mode control procedure accepted by the UE): when the SECURITY MODE COMMAND includes a NAS message container IE, the UE shall include the Replayed NAS message container IE in SECURITY MODE COMPLETE. The SECURITY MODE COMPLETE message definition/conditional-IE rules are also in clause 8.2.19.

results.question: How does the UE determine that it needs to include the replayed NAS message container?
results.reference: The UE determines this by comparing the HASHMME value received from the MME in the SECURITY MODE COMMAND message with its own locally calculated hash value during an attach or tracking area update; inclusion is triggered by a mismatch.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.21.3, Replayed NAS message container
results.model_answer: The UE does not wait for an explicit "replay" indication from the network. It correlates the received SECURITY MODE COMMAND with the NAS procedure that it initiated and determines whether that initiating NAS request must be replayed under the newly established NAS security context. Where the security-mode procedure is being performed in response to an ATTACH REQUEST, TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST, or SERVICE REQUEST, and a new/other EPS NAS security context is activated for that procedure, the UE includes the original complete initiating NAS message in the Replayed NAS message container IE of SECURITY MODE COMPLETE. The container is therefore a security-protected replay of the earlier request; it is not merely a copy of the UE security-capability IEs. The UE includes it only after successfully processing the SECURITY MODE COMMAND and activating the selected NAS security algorithms/context.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.4.3.2, "Security mode control procedure" (UE behaviour on receipt of SECURITY MODE COMMAND). This clause specifies the UE handling of SECURITY MODE COMPLETE and the condition to include the replayed NAS message container when security mode control is associated with a preceding initial EMM request/procedure and the applicable NAS security context changes. The detailed SECURITY MODE COMPLETE IE definition is in TS 24.301 clause 9.8.15.

results.question: What procedural context must be active for the condition requiring the replayed NAS message container to apply?
results.reference: The condition applies specifically during an ongoing attach procedure or an ongoing tracking area updating procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.21.3, Replayed NAS message container
results.model_answer: The condition applies only when a network-initiated security mode control procedure is being performed in the context of an ongoing attach procedure or tracking area updating procedure. In that context, the NAS message container received in SECURITY MODE COMMAND is replayed by the UE in SECURITY MODE COMPLETE; it is not a general requirement for every EMM/security-mode context.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.4.3.2 (network-initiated security mode control procedure), including the SECURITY MODE COMMAND/SECURITY MODE COMPLETE handling of the NAS message container. The condition is tied to security mode control initiated during an attach or tracking area updating procedure.

results.question: What two specific criteria must both be met for the UE to include the replayed NAS message container?
results.reference: First, the MME must have included HASHMME in the SECURITY MODE COMMAND message. Second, that received HASHMME value must differ from the hash value the UE calculated locally as per 3GPP TS 33.401.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.21.3, Replayed NAS message container
results.model_answer: The UE includes the Replayed NAS message container in SECURITY MODE COMPLETE only if both conditions are met: (1) the preceding ATTACH REQUEST or TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST was sent without NAS integrity protection; and (2) that ATTACH REQUEST or TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST included the UE network capability IE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.4.3.3 (security mode control procedure): the UE shall include the Replayed NAS message container IE in the SECURITY MODE COMPLETE message when it sent an unprotected ATTACH REQUEST or TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST and included the UE network capability IE in that request.

results.question: What must the UE check in the SECURITY MODE COMMAND before activating integrity protection for NAS messages?
results.reference: The UE must check that the integrity protection algorithm indicated in the SECURITY MODE COMMAND is not set to 'EPS integrity algorithm EIA0' and is included in its list of supported integrity protection algorithms.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.4.4, Integrity protection of NAS signalling messages
results.model_answer: Before activating NAS integrity protection, the UE must verify that the SECURITY MODE COMMAND selects NAS security algorithms supported by the UE and that the replayed UE security capabilities IE matches the capabilities previously provided by the UE (or stored for the ongoing NAS procedure). The UE must not accept a capability downgrade/mismatch. It also verifies the command's NAS integrity protection/MAC using the applicable NAS security context before acting on it.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.4.3.2 (UE behaviour on receipt of SECURITY MODE COMMAND): the UE checks whether the selected NAS security algorithms are supported and checks the replayed UE security capabilities against those sent by the UE. On mismatch it sends SECURITY MODE REJECT with cause #23, "UE security capabilities mismatch"; on unsupported/unacceptable selection it rejects security mode. After successful checks it derives/uses the selected NAS security algorithms and activates NAS integrity protection.

results.question: How should the UE proceed when lower layers indicate preparation for an S101 mode to S1 mode handover with a target cell PLMN not in forbidden lists?
results.reference: The UE shall enter substate NORMAL-SERVICE when the lower layers indicate preparation for an S101 mode to S1 mode handover and the PLMN identity of the target cell is not in any forbidden PLMN list.
results.model_answer: The UE shall initiate the tracking area updating procedure, using EPS update type "TA updating", when lower layers indicate that an S101-mode-to-S1-mode handover is being prepared and the target cell PLMN is not in the applicable forbidden-PLMN lists. The trigger occurs at handover preparation; the UE does not wait for handover completion.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.2.2 (Initiation of tracking area updating procedure): the UE is required to initiate TAU upon a lower-layer indication that an S101 mode to S1 mode handover is being prepared, subject to the target cell PLMN not being in the forbidden PLMN lists.

results.question: What is the assumed capability of the UE regarding PLMN identity determination for networks supporting cdma2000 HRPD access?
results.reference: It is assumed that the UE can determine the PLMN identity of networks supporting cdma2000 HRPD access from the information broadcast over the radio interface.
results.model_answer: It is assumed that a UE supporting cdma2000 HRPD access can determine the PLMN identity of the cdma2000 HRPD access network. The specification states this as an assumption; it does not prescribe the particular method by which the UE obtains that identity.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1 (Attach procedure, general/introductory text): note stating that a UE supporting cdma2000 HRPD access is assumed capable of determining the PLMN identity of the cdma2000 HRPD access network.

results.question: How can the PLMN identity be used for the target cell during an S101 mode to S1 mode handover involving a visited cdma2000 HRPD network?
results.reference: For the purpose of S101 mode to S1 mode handover, the UE can use the PLMN identity of the visited cdma2000 HRPD network as the PLMN identity of the target cell.
results.model_answer: Use the target E-UTRAN cell's PLMN identity as the target serving-PLMN indication for the handover. In particular, when the UE is on a visited cdma2000 HRPD network, this identity enables selection of the appropriate target-side MME/PLMN context rather than assuming that the HRPD visited-network identity is the PLMN serving the target LTE cell. It is therefore used to route/associate the S101-to-S1 handover with the MME serving the PLMN broadcast by the target cell.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.2.3, "S101 mode to S1 mode handover" (wording/numbering can vary by release). The procedure identifies the target-cell PLMN identity as information usable for selecting the appropriate MME when the handover is from a visited cdma2000 HRPD network.

results.question: Under what condition is a UE required to include the MS network capability IE when it supports A/Gb mode or Iu mode?
results.reference: The UE must include the MS network capability IE in all cases except when it is performing a periodic tracking area updating procedure.
results.model_answer: A UE that supports GERAN A/Gb mode or UTRAN Iu mode shall include the MS network capability IE when it sends an ATTACH REQUEST or a TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST. Support for either of those non-EPS access modes is the inclusion condition; it is not required solely for an E-UTRAN-only UE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clauses 5.5.1.2 (initiation of EMM attach) and 5.5.3.2 (initiation of tracking area updating): “If the UE supports A/Gb mode or Iu mode, the UE shall include the MS network capability IE” in the ATTACH REQUEST and TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST, respectively.

results.question: Why might a UE that supports either A/Gb mode or Iu mode omit the MS network capability IE in a message?
results.reference: The only permitted reason for omission is if the UE is currently executing a periodic tracking area updating procedure.
