results.model_answer: For an ATTACH REQUEST or TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST, support of A/Gb mode or Iu mode is the trigger for inclusion: the condition is a logical OR. Therefore, a UE supporting either mode should not omit the MS network capability IE merely because it supports only one of them. A valid omission is expected only when the UE supports neither A/Gb nor Iu, or when the message type/procedure does not define the IE. In an Attach/TAU trace from a UE that actually supports either mode, omission most likely indicates non-compliant implementation behavior, an incorrect capability configuration, or message decoding/version mismatch.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2.2 (ATTACH REQUEST message contents), MS network capability conditional-presence rule: the UE shall include the MS network capability IE if it supports A/Gb mode or Iu mode. The equivalent conditional rule is also specified for the TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST in clause 5.5.3.2.2.

results.question: Under what condition does the UE include the EPS bearer context status IE?
results.reference: The UE includes the EPS bearer context status IE when it wants to indicate which EPS bearer contexts are currently active within the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.33.4, EPS bearer context status
results.model_answer: The UE includes the EPS bearer context status IE in a TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST when it has one or more active EPS bearer contexts. The IE reports the UE-side activation status of EPS bearers so that the MME can reconcile bearer-context state.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.3.2 (Tracking area updating request): the UE shall include the EPS bearer context status IE in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message if it has any active EPS bearer context(s).

results.question: How does the network initiate the transport of NAS messages procedure according to clause 5.6.3.3?
results.reference: The network initiates the procedure by sending a DOWNLINK NAS TRANSPORT message to the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.6.3.3, Network initiated transport of NAS messages
results.model_answer: Per TS 24.301 clause 5.6.3.3, the network initiates the NAS-message transport procedure by sending a DOWNLINK NAS TRANSPORT message to the UE. The message carries the NAS payload in its payload container (with the applicable payload-container type); the UE processes/delivers that container to the appropriate upper-layer entity. NAS security protection is applied as required by the active EMM security context and NAS security rules.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.6.3.3 (Network initiated transport of NAS messages): the network initiates transport of NAS messages by sending a DOWNLINK NAS TRANSPORT message to the UE.

results.question: Under what specific EPS service condition can the network initiate downlink NAS transport even without PDN connections?
results.reference: When the UE is using EPS services with control plane CIoT EPS optimization, the network can initiate the procedure even if the UE does not have any PDN connections established.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.6.3.3, Network initiated transport of NAS messages
results.model_answer: The exception is emergency bearer service: the network may initiate downlink NAS transport without any existing PDN connection when it is initiating ESM procedures for emergency bearer services (i.e., for a UE attached/registered for emergency bearer services). This is not a general permission for normal EPS services without a PDN connection.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.6.3 (Downlink NAS transport procedure; read with clause 5.6.1 general rules): the normal PDN-connection precondition for network-initiated downlink NAS transport has an exception for initiation of ESM procedures for emergency bearer services.

results.question: Under what conditions must a network include the packet flow identifier IE when supporting mobility from S1 mode to A/Gb mode?
results.reference: The network must include the packet flow identifier IE only if the UE supports both A/Gb mode and BSS packet flow procedures.
results.model_answer: The network shall include the packet flow identifier (PFI) IE when both conditions are met: (1) the network supports mobility from S1 mode to A/Gb mode; and (2) the UE has indicated support for “S1 mode to A/Gb mode mobility” in the UE network capability IE. If either condition is not met, this mandatory-inclusion condition does not apply.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.4.1.2 (default EPS bearer context activation initiated by the network): the network is required to include the PFI IE under the conjunction of network support for S1-to-A/Gb mobility and UE indication of that mobility capability. The corresponding dedicated-bearer procedure has the same principle in clause 6.4.2.2.

results.question: What are the two UE capabilities that must be present for the network to include the packet flow identifier IE during mobility from S1 mode to A/Gb mode?
results.reference: The UE must support A/Gb mode and BSS packet flow procedures.
results.model_answer: The UE must indicate both (1) support for S1-mode-to-A/Gb-mode mobility and (2) packet flow identifier (PFI) support. The first capability is conveyed in the UE network capability; PFI support is conveyed in the MS network capability. Only when both are indicated may/shall the network include the PFI IE for this mobility case.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause covering mobility from S1 mode to A/Gb mode (most likely §5.5.3.2, Tracking Area Updating / inter-RAT mobility handling): the PFI IE inclusion condition is tied to the UE indication of both S1 mode to A/Gb mode mobility support and PFI support.

results.question: Why might a UE initiate the tracking area updating procedure after an inter-system change from S101 mode to S1 mode?
results.reference: The procedure is initiated after such an inter-system change if the UE has no user data pending, as specified by condition (d) in the clause.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.3.2.2, Normal and periodic tracking area updating procedure initiation
results.model_answer: An inter-system change from S101 mode to S1 mode is itself a specified UE trigger for tracking area updating. On return to S1/E-UTRAN access, the UE performs TAU so that the MME can refresh the UE's EPS mobility/location registration and apply the current S1-mode context (for example, current TAI/TAI list and reachability). This trigger can apply independently of the ordinary condition that the UE has entered a TAI outside its registered TAI list.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.3.2 ("Initiation of tracking area updating procedure"): the UE is specified to initiate TAU after an inter-system change from S101 mode to S1 mode.

results.question: Under what conditions may a UE include the Requested WUS assistance information IE?
results.reference: The UE may include this IE if it supports WUS assistance and it is not attaching for emergency bearer services.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.29.33, Requested WUS assistance information
results.model_answer: A UE may include the Requested WUS assistance information IE in an ATTACH REQUEST or TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST when it supports wake-up signal (WUS) operation and is requesting/using eDRX. The IE is optional and is used when the UE requests WUS assistance information from the MME; it is not applicable as a general-purpose IE in unrelated NAS procedures. The UE's WUS/eDRX capability and the eDRX-related request/configuration provide the relevant basis for including it.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clauses: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2 (contents/procedures for ATTACH REQUEST) and clause 5.5.3.2 (contents/procedures for TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST), including the conditional-presence rules for the Requested WUS assistance information IE. The corresponding IE definition is in TS 24.301 clause 9.9 (information elements), under Requested WUS assistance information.

results.question: What are the two prerequisites that must be satisfied for a UE to include the Requested WUS assistance information IE?
results.reference: The UE must support WUS assistance and the attachment must not be for emergency bearer services.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.29.33, Requested WUS assistance information
results.model_answer: The UE includes the Requested WUS assistance information IE only when both conditions hold: (1) the UE supports Wake-Up Signal (WUS), and (2) the UE is configured to use eDRX. WUS assistance is tied to eDRX operation; WUS capability alone is not sufficient.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, UE NAS message-construction requirements for the Requested WUS assistance information IE (notably the ATTACH REQUEST / TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST procedure text in clauses 5.5.2.2 and 5.5.3.2): the inclusion condition is expressed conjunctively for a UE that supports WUS and is configured to use eDRX.

results.question: In which scenario is a UE prohibited from including the Requested WUS assistance information IE?
results.reference: When the UE is attaching for emergency bearer services, it is prohibited from including this IE, regardless of its WUS assistance support.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.29.33, Requested WUS assistance information
results.model_answer: A UE is prohibited from including the Requested WUS assistance information IE when it sends an ATTACH REQUEST with the attach type set to "EPS emergency attach".
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2.2 (ATTACH REQUEST message contents). The emergency-attach-specific rules prohibit inclusion of the Requested WUS assistance information IE for an EPS emergency attach.

results.question: What is the primary purpose of sending an EMM STATUS message according to the 3GPP specification?
results.reference: The primary purpose is to report certain error conditions detected upon receipt of EMM protocol data at any time.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.7, Reception of an EMM STATUS message by an EMM entity
results.model_answer: The primary purpose of an EMM STATUS message is to report an EMM error condition between the UE and the MME; it is an error-reporting procedure, not a normal registration, mobility-management, or bearer-control procedure.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.7.1 (EMM status procedure, General): "The purpose of the EMM status procedure is to report an EMM error condition."

results.question: What does the specification state about which entities are permitted to send an EMM STATUS message?
results.reference: The EMM STATUS message can be sent by both the MME and the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.7, Reception of an EMM STATUS message by an EMM entity
results.model_answer: An EMM STATUS message may be sent only by the UE or by the MME. TS 24.301 defines the EMM status procedure as being initiable by either entity, with EMM STATUS used to report EMM error/abnormal conditions; it is not a message sent by eNB or other EPS entities.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.7.1 (EMM status procedure — General): the EMM status procedure can be initiated by the UE or the MME, and the EMM STATUS message is sent by the UE or the MME to report an EMM error condition.

results.question: According to the clause, what determines the local actions taken by the MME or UE upon receipt of an EMM STATUS message?
results.reference: The local actions to be taken are implementation dependent.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.7, Reception of an EMM STATUS message by an EMM entity
results.model_answer: The local actions are determined by the EMM cause value contained in the received EMM STATUS message.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.7.1 (EMM status procedure — General): "Upon receipt of an EMM STATUS message, the MME or the UE shall take local actions depending on the EMM cause value received in the EMM STATUS message."

results.question: Why might a receiver ignore an entire NAS message during processing, and what subsequent action is required?
results.reference: A receiver shall ignore the entire NAS message if it contains a syntactically incorrect mandatory IE, a message type not defined for the protocol, or a protocol discriminator not indicating NAS. The receiver must then take no further action and discard the message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 7, Handling of unknown, unforeseen, and erroneous protocol data
results.model_answer: A receiver may ignore the whole NAS message when a protocol error prevents reliable interpretation, notably an incorrect message length or missing/invalid mandatory information element(s). It shall normally send a NAS STATUS message with EMM cause #96, "invalid mandatory information." A received STATUS message is not answered with another STATUS message, to avoid a STATUS loop. Other whole-message errors use their corresponding STATUS cause (for example, #97 for an unsupported message type or #99 for an unimplemented comprehension-required IE).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.4.3 (handling of unknown, unforeseen and erroneous protocol data), especially the subclauses for missing mandatory IEs, incorrect message length, and incorrect mandatory IE contents: the receiver ignores the message and returns STATUS with cause #96 "invalid mandatory information," except that STATUS itself is not answered by STATUS.

results.question: How does the ESM information request procedure provide privacy for ESM information?
results.reference: By allowing the network to retrieve the ESM information from the UE after ciphering is enabled, ensuring the information is sent security protected.
results.model_answer: The UE can defer disclosure of sensitive ESM information—principally the APN and protocol configuration options (PCO)—from the initial PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST. It indicates support/use of ESM information transfer, and the network later sends an ESM INFORMATION REQUEST after NAS security activation. The UE returns the APN/PCO in an ESM INFORMATION RESPONSE protected by NAS ciphering (and integrity protection), so those values are not exposed in clear text on the initial access signalling.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.5.1 (ESM information request procedure): the procedure allows the network to request ESM information, such as APN and PCO, after security procedures have been completed, thereby avoiding transmission of this information in clear text. The associated ESM INFORMATION REQUEST/RESPONSE handling requires NAS security protection where a security context is available/activated.

results.question: Under what condition does the network use the ESM information request procedure to retrieve information from the UE?
results.reference: When the UE indicated in the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message that it has ESM information that needs to be sent security protected.
results.model_answer: The network uses the ESM information request procedure only during a PDN connectivity procedure, when it requires ESM information from the UE before it can initiate establishment of the PDN connection (for example, APN and/or protocol configuration options not otherwise available to the network).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.5.1 (ESM information request procedure — General): the procedure is initiated by the network to retrieve ESM information from the UE and can be initiated during the PDN connectivity procedure when the network requires that information before initiating PDN connection establishment.

results.question: What specific types of ESM information can the network retrieve using the ESM information request procedure?
results.reference: Protocol configuration options, APN, or both.
results.model_answer: The network can retrieve the UE's access point name (APN), protocol configuration options (PCO), and—when supported—extended protocol configuration options (EPCO). These are the ESM parameters needed by the network to select/configure the PDN connection; the procedure is not used to obtain bearer QoS or the UE IP address.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.5.5 (ESM information request procedure), especially the general/network-initiated procedure text: the network requests ESM information from the UE, namely the APN and protocol configuration options; later releases also support transfer of extended protocol configuration options. See also the ESM INFORMATION RESPONSE message definition in TS 24.301 clause 8.3.19, which carries the APN, PCO, and, where applicable, EPCO IEs.

results.question: What type of information element is the Additional information, and what is its minimum length?
results.reference: It is a type 4 information element with a minimum length of 3 octets.
results.model_answer: The Additional information IE is a Type 4 (TLV) information element. Its minimum total length is 3 octets (1-octet IEI, 1-octet length field, and at least 1 octet of information content).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.2 (Additional information): the clause identifies it as a type 4 information element with a minimum length of 3 octets.

results.question: On what factor does the coding of the additional information value depend?
results.reference: The coding of the additional information value is dependent on the generic message container type.
results.model_answer: The coding of the Additional information value depends on the EMM cause value.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.3.1 (Additional information): "The coding of the additional information value depends on the EMM cause value."

results.question: What procedure shall the UE perform when the NO-CELL-AVAILABLE condition is encountered?
results.reference: The UE shall perform cell selection/reselection.
results.model_answer: The UE shall enter the EMM-DEREGISTERED.NO-CELL-AVAILABLE substate and perform PLMN selection in accordance with 3GPP TS 23.122, until a suitable or acceptable cell is found. It shall not initiate normal NAS registration procedures while no cell is available.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.3.1.3 (EMM-DEREGISTERED.NO-CELL-AVAILABLE): this substate applies when the UE cannot find a suitable or acceptable cell under TS 23.122; the UE performs PLMN selection according to TS 23.122.

results.question: According to which specification shall the UE conduct cell selection/reselection in the NO-CELL-AVAILABLE scenario?
results.reference: The UE shall perform it according to 3GPP TS 36.304 [21].
results.model_answer: The UE shall conduct E-UTRA cell selection and reselection according to 3GPP TS 36.304.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.1.1.2, EMM-DEREGISTERED.NO-CELL-AVAILABLE substate: the UE performs PLMN selection and cell selection/reselection in accordance with 3GPP TS 23.122 and 3GPP TS 36.304, respectively.

results.question: What actions must a UE take upon the first expiry of timer T3482 when the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST was sent with request type set to 'handover of emergency bearer services' in a stand-alone PDN connectivity procedure?
results.reference: The UE shall either inform the upper layers of the failure to establish the emergency bearer, or detach locally (if not already detached) and attempt EPS attach for emergency bearer services.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.5.1.5, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: On the first expiry of T3482, the UE shall retransmit the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST, but change its request type from "handover of emergency bearer services" to "emergency request". The UE shall then restart T3482. It does not abort the PDN connectivity procedure at this first expiry.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.5.2.2 (UE-requested/stand-alone PDN connectivity procedure), T3482 expiry handling: the special first-expiry rule for a PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST whose request type is "handover of emergency bearer services" requires retransmission with request type set to "emergency request", followed by restarting T3482.

results.question: How many times can a UE retransmit the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message upon expiry of timer T3482 for a non-emergency request before aborting the procedure?
results.reference: The UE can retransmit the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST four times. On the fifth expiry of timer T3482, the UE shall abort the procedure, release the PTI, and enter PROCEDURE TRANSACTION INACTIVE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.5.1.5, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: 5 times. For a non-emergency PDN connectivity request, the UE retransmits the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST on T3482 expiry; after the fifth expiry of T3482, it aborts the PDN connectivity procedure. The initial transmission is separate from these timer-expiry retransmissions.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, UE-requested PDN connectivity procedure, T3482 expiry handling: the UE retransmits the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST and restarts T3482; it shall abort the PDN connectivity procedure after the fifth expiry of T3482. The emergency-bearer case is handled differently and is aborted on expiry rather than retried.

results.question: Why can a SECURITY PROTECTED NAS MESSAGE not be included in the IE that contains a complete plain NAS message?
results.reference: Because the clause explicitly states that the SECURITY PROTECTED NAS MESSAGE is not a plain NAS message and shall not be included in this IE.
results.model_answer: Because the container is defined to carry an embedded plain NAS message, not a second NAS PDU with its own security header. NAS integrity protection/ciphering, NAS COUNT and replay protection are applied and verified at the outer NAS-message level. A SECURITY PROTECTED NAS MESSAGE inside the container would introduce nested and independently scoped security processing, including a second security header and COUNT/MAC context, which the container decoding procedure does not support. Therefore TS 24.301 normatively prohibits it; protection, when applicable, is provided by the outer SECURITY PROTECTED NAS MESSAGE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.3 (NAS message container IE; exact subclause numbering is release-dependent): the IE "shall contain a complete plain NAS message" and "shall not contain a SECURITY PROTECTED NAS MESSAGE." Relevant security architecture is specified in clause 4.4.3, Security protected NAS message.

results.question: What requirements must a NAS message meet to be validly included in this IE?
results.reference: The NAS message must be a complete plain NAS message as specified in clauses 8.2 and 8.3 of TS 24.301.
results.model_answer: The ESM message container IE must carry one complete, syntactically valid ESM NAS message, including its ESM header. It cannot contain only ESM payload/IEs, a fragment of an ESM message, or an independently NAS-security-protected inner NAS PDU. The IE length must equal the octet length of the encapsulated complete ESM message; NAS security, when applicable, is applied to the enclosing NAS message.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9, "ESM message container" IE definition (most likely evidence clause): the IE is used to encapsulate an ESM message and shall contain a complete ESM message as specified for ESM messages. The relevant ESM message format/header requirements are specified in TS 24.301 clause 6.3.

results.question: What is the primary purpose of the EPS AKA procedure as defined in the clause?
results.reference: The primary purpose is to provide mutual authentication between the user and the network and to agree on a key KASME.
results.model_answer: The EPS AKA procedure primarily provides mutual authentication between the UE and the EPS network and establishes fresh keying material/security context for protecting NAS communications.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.1.1 (Authentication and key agreement — General): EPS AKA is used to authenticate the UE and network and to derive/establish the security keys used for EPS NAS security.

results.question: How is the EPS AKA procedure initiated and controlled, and what capability does the UE have regarding it?
results.reference: The EPS AKA procedure is always initiated and controlled by the network. However, the UE can reject the EPS authentication challenge sent by the network.
results.model_answer: The EPS AKA procedure is initiated by the network, specifically by sending an AUTHENTICATION REQUEST to the UE. It is network-controlled; the UE responds according to the received authentication parameters and does not initiate EPS AKA itself. The UE is required to support EPS AKA.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.1.1 (EPS authentication and key agreement procedure): "The EPS AKA procedure is always initiated by the network and controlled by the network. The UE shall support EPS AKA."

results.question: Under what condition must the UE proceed with an EPS authentication challenge?
results.reference: The UE shall proceed with an EPS authentication challenge only if a USIM is present.
results.model_answer: The UE shall proceed with the EPS authentication challenge only if it successfully verifies the AUTN received in the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST. In EPS AKA, this means that the AUTN MAC verification succeeds and the sequence number (SQN) is acceptable; otherwise the UE sends AUTHENTICATION FAILURE (e.g., MAC failure or synchronization failure).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.4.2.2 (Authentication request): after successful verification of the AUTN parameter, the UE shall proceed with the EPS authentication challenge.

results.question: What is established and how is the key KASME derived and used during a successful EPS authentication procedure?
results.reference: A partial native EPS security context is established. The CK and IK are computed by the USIM, then used by the ME as key material to compute KASME. KASME is stored in the EPS security contexts and in the ME's volatile memory, serving as the root for the EPS integrity protection and ciphering key hierarchy.
results.model_answer: In a successful EPS AKA run, the UE authenticates the serving network by validating AUTN, the network authenticates the UE by validating RES against XRES, and both sides obtain the same EPS anchor key KASME. KASME is not sent over NAS. The UE derives it from the AKA outputs CK and IK and from serving-network- and sequence-number-bound inputs: KASME = KDF(CK||IK, FC=0x10 || SN-id || L(SN-id) || (SQN xor AK) || L(SQN xor AK)). The UE obtains CK, IK and AK from USIM AKA functions; the MME normally receives the corresponding KASME in the authentication vector from the HSS. KASME is then the root key for deriving NAS integrity and ciphering keys (K_NASint and K_NASenc) and, via further derivation, access-stratum keys. The NAS security mode control procedure selects algorithms and activates use of the derived NAS keys; successful authentication alone supplies/authenticates the key material but does not by itself mean that NAS ciphering/integrity protection is already active.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, §5.1.1.3, "Authentication procedure by the UE"—on successful network authentication the UE calculates RES and derives KASME as specified in TS 33.401. The KASME derivation and its key-hierarchy use are specified more directly in 3GPP TS 33.401 §6.1.1 and Annex A.2; derivation of NAS keys is in TS 33.401 §6.2.1. NAS security-mode activation behavior is in TS 24.301 §5.4.2.

results.question: What procedures must a UE execute when its configuration on use of SMS changes while operating in PS mode 1 or PS mode 2, and the change is to 'SMS service is not preferred to be invoked over IP networks' or the UE becomes unable to use SMS using IMS?
results.reference: The UE shall transit from PS mode 1 to CS/PS mode 1 or from PS mode 2 to CS/PS mode 2, and perform a combined tracking area update with IMSI attach, which may include 'SMS only'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.3.2.5, Change of configuration regarding the use of SMS.
results.model_answer: The UE shall initiate a tracking area updating (TAU) procedure to notify the EPS/MME of the changed SMS-over-IP preference/capability. This applies when, in PS mode 1 or PS mode 2, the UE changes to "SMS service is not preferred to be invoked over IP networks" or can no longer use SMS over IMS/IP. The TAU shall convey the updated UE capability/preference information; no separate EPS detach or re-attach is required solely for this change.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.3.3.1 (General — initiation of the tracking area updating procedure). The TAU-initiation conditions include a UE configuration change concerning use of SMS over IP networks, including change from SMS-over-IP preferred to not preferred and inability to use SMS over IP networks, for a UE operating in PS mode 1 or PS mode 2.

results.question: What actions are required for a UE in CS/PS mode 1 or CS/PS mode 2 when the configuration changes to prefer SMS over IP networks, the UE can use SMS via IMS, and the voice domain preference for E-UTRAN is 'IMS PS voice only'?
results.reference: The UE shall transit from CS/PS mode 1 to PS mode 1 or from CS/PS mode 2 to PS mode 2, and perform a detach for non-EPS services.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.3.2.5, Change of configuration regarding the use of SMS.
results.model_answer: The UE shall initiate a tracking area updating procedure to report the changed SMS transport preference to the EPS network. The TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST shall include the Voice domain preference and UE's usage setting IE, carrying the SMS-over-IP-network preference as configured. This applies to a UE in CS/PS mode 1 or CS/PS mode 2 when it supports SMS via IMS and its E-UTRAN voice-domain preference is "IMS PS voice only".
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.3.3.1 (general rules for initiation of the tracking area updating procedure): a change of the configured preference for SMS over IP networks, under the stated IMS-SMS-capable and "IMS PS voice only" conditions, requires the UE to perform TAU. The associated preference is conveyed in the Voice domain preference and UE's usage setting IE; see TS 24.301 clause 9.9.3.44.

results.question: What is the purpose of the PDN type information element as defined in the clause?
results.reference: The purpose is to indicate either the IP version capability of the IP stack associated with the UE, or to indicate non-IP.
results.model_answer: The PDN type information element indicates the type of PDN connection requested by the UE (for example, IPv4, IPv6, IPv4v6, or other standardized PDN types where applicable).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.4.10 (PDN type): "The purpose of the PDN type information element is to indicate the type of PDN connection requested by the UE."

results.question: What types of protocol data examples are given for transmission using the Extended protocol configuration options IE?
results.reference: Examples include configuration parameters, error codes, or messages/events.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.10.8, Extended protocol configuration options
results.model_answer: The examples are PPP protocol data, 3GPP-specific protocol data, and other protocol data. They are illustrative categories, not an exhaustive list.
results.evidence: Most likely clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 10.5.6.3A, "Extended protocol configuration options". The clause describes the IE as being usable to transfer, for example, PPP protocol data, 3GPP-specific protocol data, and other protocol data.

results.question: Under what specific condition during the attach procedure must a UE include the ESM information transfer flag in the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message?
results.reference: The UE must include it when it has protocol configuration options that require security-protected transfer or when it wants to provide an access point name for the PDN connection being established.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.20.2, ESM information transfer flag
results.model_answer: During an attach, the UE shall include the ESM information transfer flag in the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST when it needs to transfer ESM information (for example, APN and/or protocol configuration options) to the network after completion of the EMM procedure. The flag is set to indicate that ESM information transfer is required, causing the network to request that information later.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.5.1.2 (UE-requested PDN connectivity): when the UE is performing an attach procedure, it shall include the ESM information transfer flag IE in the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message if it needs to transfer ESM information to the network after the EMM procedure has been completed.

results.question: How does the UE indicate the need to securely transfer protocol configuration options during the attach procedure?
results.reference: By including the ESM information transfer flag in the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message sent during the attach procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.20.2, ESM information transfer flag
results.model_answer: The UE sets the ESM information transfer flag in the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST (carried in the ATTACH REQUEST's ESM message container) to "ESM information transfer required". This tells the network that PCO (and, if applicable, the APN) is to be provided later, after NAS security activation, in an ESM INFORMATION RESPONSE.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2 (UE-initiated attach procedure): when the UE needs to transfer ESM information, such as APN and/or protocol configuration options, securely after NAS security establishment, it shall set the ESM information transfer flag in the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST to "ESM information transfer required". See also clause 5.10.3 (PDN connectivity procedure) and the ESM information transfer flag IE definition in clause 9.9.4.2.

results.question: What are the two distinct reasons that would compel a UE to include the ESM information transfer flag in the initial PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST?
results.reference: Either to transfer protocol configuration options with security protection or to supply an access point name for the PDN connection being set up.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.20.2, ESM information transfer flag
results.model_answer: The two triggers are: (1) the UE needs to provide the APN, and (2) the UE needs to provide Protocol Configuration Options (PCO), but defers either or both from the initial PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST. In that case it sets the ESM information transfer flag so that the network obtains the deferred APN and/or PCO through the ESM information transfer procedure (ESM INFORMATION REQUEST/RESPONSE).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.5.1.2 (PDN connectivity procedure initiation): the UE includes the ESM information transfer flag in the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST when it needs to transfer ESM information, i.e. an APN and/or protocol configuration options, using the ESM information transfer procedure.

results.question: In which message and during which procedure does the UE use the ESM information transfer flag to provide an APN for the PDN connection?
results.reference: In the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message sent as part of the attach procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.20.2, ESM information transfer flag
results.model_answer: The UE sets the ESM information transfer flag in the ESM PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST (often carried inside an ATTACH REQUEST for an initial PDN connection). This indicates that APN/PCO information will be transferred separately. The UE then provides the APN in the ESM INFORMATION RESPONSE message, sent in the ESM information transfer procedure after the network sends an ESM INFORMATION REQUEST.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.5.1 (ESM information transfer procedure), especially clause 6.5.1.2: the UE responds to ESM INFORMATION REQUEST with ESM INFORMATION RESPONSE and includes the APN when applicable. The triggering indication is the ESM information transfer flag in PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST, specified in clause 6.5.2.1 and the ESM information transfer flag IE definition.

results.question: What are the two main aspects of security protection for EPS NAS messages between UE and MME as described in the general principles?
results.reference: Integrity protection and ciphering of the EMM and ESM NAS messages.
results.model_answer: The two main aspects are: (1) integrity protection of EPS NAS messages, to detect modification/replay and authenticate message origin; and (2) ciphering of EPS NAS messages, to provide confidentiality of NAS signalling contents.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 4.4.1 (General principles), states that security protection for EPS NAS messages between the UE and MME consists of two main aspects: integrity protection and ciphering.

results.question: How is the operation of a network without ciphering achieved according to the note in the clause?
results.reference: By configuring the MME to always select the 'null ciphering algorithm', EEA0.
results.model_answer: The network operates without NAS ciphering by selecting EEA0 (the null ciphering algorithm) as the NAS ciphering algorithm in the SECURITY MODE COMMAND. EEA0 causes NAS messages to be sent without encryption; this does not by itself disable NAS integrity protection, which is selected independently.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 4.4.5 (security mode control), note stating in substance: "The operation of a network without ciphering is achieved by using the ciphering algorithm EEA0."

results.question: Where are the detailed signalling procedures for the control of NAS security described?
results.reference: They are part of the EMM protocol and are described in detail in clause 5.
results.model_answer: In 3GPP TS 24.301, the detailed signalling procedures for control of NAS security are described in clause 5.4.4, "Security mode control procedure."
results.evidence: TS 24.301 clause 4.4.1 (NAS security general provisions) directs the reader to clause 5.4.4 for the detailed signalling procedures controlling NAS security.

results.question: What does clause 4.4.1 describe regarding EPS security contexts?
results.reference: The principles for handling EPS security contexts in the UE and in the MME.
results.model_answer: Clause 4.4.1 defines the EPS security context used for NAS security between the UE and MME. It distinguishes a native EPS security context, created following EPS AKA, from a mapped EPS security context, derived by mapping a non-EPS/UMTS security context. The context is identified by the eKSI and provides the keying material, selected NAS integrity/ciphering algorithms, derived NAS keys, and associated NAS COUNT/state needed to protect NAS signalling.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 4.4.1 ("EPS security context"): describes EPS security-context establishment and use, including native versus mapped EPS security contexts and their identification/association with NAS security parameters.

results.question: Under what condition is the APN-AMBR information element included in a message from the network to the UE?
results.reference: When the network wishes to transmit the APN-AMBR to the UE for possible uplink policy enforcement.
results.model_answer: The network includes APN-AMBR in an ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST when the UE needs to be provided with the APN-level aggregate maximum bit rate for that APN—i.e., when no applicable APN-AMBR is already available at the UE, or when the APN-AMBR value has changed. The IE may also be conveyed during bearer-context modification to update a previously supplied value.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.4.1.1 (default EPS bearer context activation, general), read with clause 9.9.4.2 (APN-AMBR IE). These specify the network-to-UE delivery of APN-AMBR for the APN associated with the PDN connection and its UE storage/use; a new or changed APN-AMBR must therefore be sent to the UE.

results.question: What is the purpose of the network including the APN-AMBR IE in a message sent to the UE?
results.reference: To provide the APN-AMBR to the UE so it can potentially enforce uplink policy.
results.model_answer: The APN-AMBR IE informs the UE of the authorized aggregate maximum bit rate for non-GBR EPS bearers associated with the APN (separate uplink and downlink limits). The UE stores this APN-specific value and uses it as the rate limit applicable to aggregate non-GBR traffic for that APN; it is not a per-bearer GBR/QoS value.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.4.2 (APN-AMBR): the IE is used to indicate the APN-AMBR for the APN, with the APN-AMBR defined in TS 23.401. Relevant EPS bearer-context activation procedures (TS 24.301 clause 6.4.1) specify delivery/handling of APN-AMBR in network-to-UE bearer activation signalling.

results.question: For what potential UE-side action does the network transmit the APN-AMBR?
results.reference: For the UE to possibly enforce uplink policy based on the received APN-AMBR.
results.model_answer: The network transmits the APN-AMBR so that the UE may perform traffic shaping/rate control for traffic associated with that APN, i.e. constrain the aggregate non-GBR traffic rate to the APN-level authorized maximum.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.4.1.1 (Default EPS bearer context activation — General): the APN-AMBR is provided by the network to the UE and may be used by the UE for traffic shaping.

results.question: How does the clause describe the network's intent when including the APN-AMBR information element?
results.reference: The network includes it when it wishes to send the APN-AMBR to the UE for potential uplink policy enforcement.
results.model_answer: Including the APN-AMBR IE signals that the network is providing the APN aggregate maximum bit rate applicable to the PDN connection's APN. In a bearer-modification context, its inclusion specifically signals a change to that APN-AMBR. It is an APN/PDN-connection aggregate limit, not a per-EPS-bearer QoS/GBR indication.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.4.1 (APN aggregate maximum bit rate). The clause describes the IE as indicating the APN-AMBR for the APN associated with the PDN connection; when used in MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST, it indicates a change in the APN-AMBR.

results.question: Under what specific UE mode and condition must the UE include the NAS message container IE?
results.reference: The UE must include the NAS message container IE when it is in EMM-IDLE mode and has pending SMS messages to be sent.
results.model_answer: The UE shall include the NAS message container IE when it is in ECM-IDLE mode, uses the Control Plane CIoT EPS optimisation, and has uplink user data to send. The IE carries the ESM DATA TRANSPORT message in the CONTROL PLANE SERVICE REQUEST.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.11.3 (Control plane CIoT EPS optimisation), in the UE-initiated control-plane service-request behaviour; see also the CONTROL PLANE SERVICE REQUEST message definition in clause 8.2.30 and the NAS message container IE definition in clause 9.9.2.5.

results.question: In which operational state must the UE be, and what must be pending, for it to include the NAS message container IE?
results.reference: The UE must be in the EMM-IDLE operational state and must have pending SMS messages to be sent.
results.model_answer: The UE must be in EMM-IDLE mode and have a pending ESM procedure. The NAS message container is used to piggyback the pending ESM request, e.g. a PDN connectivity, PDN disconnect, bearer-resource allocation, or bearer-resource modification request, in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.3.2 (tracking area updating procedure initiation). It specifies inclusion of the NAS message container in a TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST when the UE is in EMM-IDLE and an ESM procedure/request is pending. The corresponding TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST message definition and NAS message container IE rules are in clause 9.9.

results.question: Under what conditions does the UE initiate a tracking area updating procedure when timer T3411 expires?
results.reference: The UE shall initiate a tracking area updating procedure on the expiry of timer T3411 as part of normal service operation.
results.model_answer: T3411 is the retry/attempting-to-update timer. On its expiry, the UE initiates a new tracking area updating procedure when it is still in EMM-REGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE (i.e., a previous TAU attempt was aborted/failed and the UE still needs to update). This is not an unconditional TAU trigger in every EMM state; normal cell-selection, service-availability, access-barring, and any applicable back-off/prohibition conditions still govern whether the UE can actually send the TAU REQUEST.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.3.2 (TAU procedure initiation/abnormal handling): the normative T3411-expiry behavior is that, upon expiry of T3411, the UE in EMM-REGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-UPDATE shall initiate the tracking area updating procedure. T3411 is defined as controlling the time between tracking area updating attempts.

results.question: What implementation option is specified for a MUSIM UE regarding its response to paging during normal service?
results.reference: As an implementation option, the MUSIM UE is allowed to not respond to paging based on information available in the paging message, such as voice service indication.
results.model_answer: For a MUSIM UE, responding to a paging request during normal service is an implementation option. In particular, when simultaneous handling of subscriptions is not possible (for example, another USIM is using the radio), the UE may choose not to respond to the paging for the paged subscription; if it does respond, it uses the normal NAS Service Request procedure.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.3.4.1 (Service request procedure — General). The MUSIM-specific text makes the response to a paging request during normal service an implementation option, rather than an unconditional requirement applicable to a single-subscription UE.

results.question: What specific action must a UE configured for eCall only mode take at the expiry of timers T3444 or T3445?
results.reference: If configured for eCall only mode, the UE shall perform the eCall inactivity procedure at the expiry of timer T3444 or T3445.
results.model_answer: At expiry of either T3444 or T3445, a UE configured for eCall-only mode shall enter the EMM-DEREGISTERED.ECALL-INACTIVE state (i.e., cease the registered eCall-only operating state).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.3.12 (eCall only mode): the eCall-only-mode procedure specifies that expiry of T3444 or T3445 causes the UE to enter EMM-DEREGISTERED.ECALL-INACTIVE.

results.question: What is the primary purpose of the mobility management sublayer in EMM procedures?
results.reference: The primary purpose is to support user equipment mobility, specifically by informing the network of its present location and providing user identity confidentiality.
results.model_answer: The mobility-management function of EMM primarily maintains the UE's EPS registration and reachability as it moves between tracking areas—i.e., it performs mobility-related control such as attach, tracking-area update, detach and service request. EMM also manages NAS security, but mobility/location registration is its central purpose.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.1 (EPS mobility management): EMM procedures are used to support UE mobility and to manage the security context between the UE and the network.

results.question: How does the EMM sublayer interact with other sublayers and entities?
results.reference: It provides connection management services to the session management (SM) sublayer and the short message services (SMS) entity of the connection management (CM) sublayer.
results.model_answer: The EMM sublayer is the NAS mobility-control sublayer, terminated between the UE and the MME. It provides mobility, registration/attach, reachability/service-request, detach, authentication and NAS-security control. It provides an EMM service to the ESM sublayer through the EMM service access point: ESM uses EMM connectivity/security and may have ESM procedure messages transported with, or in the context of, EMM procedures. Toward the access stratum, EMM uses the NAS transport service supplied by lower layers (normally RRC/PDCP over E-UTRAN) to exchange NAS messages with its peer EMM entity. Interactions with eNB, HSS, SGW, etc. are MME/UE implementation or inter-node procedures, not direct standardized EMM-to-entity NAS interfaces in TS 24.301.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 4.2 (NAS protocol architecture/protocol stack; clause title and numbering can vary slightly by release): NAS is divided into the EMM and ESM sublayers, and the EMM sublayer provides an EMM service to the ESM sublayer. The same architectural material identifies NAS as a UE-to-MME protocol and shows its use of lower-layer/AS transport.

results.question: What specific delay consideration is noted for satellite E-UTRAN access regarding initial uplink NAS messages?
results.reference: In satellite access, a GNSS fix time in lower layers can delay transmission of an initial uplink NAS message by up to 100 seconds when in a GNSS cold state.
results.model_answer: For satellite E-UTRAN access, the UE is expected to account for the substantially longer satellite propagation delay for delivery of an initial uplink NAS message and for receipt of the network response. Thus, normal terrestrial assumptions about prompt completion/reply to an initial NAS message should not be used; the satellite link delay has to be allowed for when applying the relevant NAS procedure/timer behavior. The note is qualitative—TS 24.301 does not define a separate fixed NAS delay value solely for this purpose.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.1 (General for attach / initial NAS-message handling), note concerning satellite E-UTRAN access: it notes that the transmission/delivery of an initial uplink NAS message can be subject to satellite delay. Related procedure clauses for TAU and service request use the same initial-NAS-message and NAS-timer principles.

results.question: Under what specific conditions is the UE required to include the GPRS ciphering key sequence number IE?
results.reference: The UE must include the IE when it performs an inter-system change from either A/Gb mode or Iu mode to S1 mode while in EMM-IDLE mode, and when its Temporary Identity used in Next update (TIN) indicates "P-TMSI".
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.29.3, GPRS ciphering key sequence number
results.model_answer: The UE shall include the GPRS ciphering key sequence number (CKSN) IE when it performs a combined EPS/non-EPS registration procedure: (1) in an ATTACH REQUEST for a combined EPS/IMSI attach, and (2) in a TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST for a combined TA/LA update (including the combined TA/LA update with IMSI attach variant). It is not required for EPS-only attach or EPS-only TAU. The condition is the combined-procedure type, not merely whether a valid GPRS ciphering key exists; if the applicable procedure requires the IE and no valid GPRS key is available, the IE uses the 'no key available' indication.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clauses: 3GPP TS 24.301, §5.5.1.2 (UE behaviour for ATTACH REQUEST) and §5.5.3.2 (UE behaviour for TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST), read with §9.9.3.12 (GPRS ciphering key sequence number IE). These clauses specify inclusion for combined attach/combined tracking-area updating and define the IE's key-sequence/no-key-available semantics.

results.question: Under what three specific conditions must the network include the Negotiated WUS assistance information IE?
results.reference: The network must include the IE when: 1) the UE supports WUS assistance, 2) the MME supports and accepts the use of WUS assistance, and 3) the UE is not attaching for emergency bearer services.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.26.27, Negotiated WUS assistance information
results.model_answer: The network shall include the Negotiated WUS assistance information IE when all three apply: (1) the UE is in NB-S1 mode, (2) the UE indicated WUS support in the UE network capability IE, and (3) the UE included a WUS assistance information IE in its ATTACH REQUEST (or the corresponding TAU request context).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2.2 (ATTACH ACCEPT), in the WUS-assistance-information handling text; the corresponding TAU-accept handling is specified in clause 5.5.3.2.4. The requirement is scoped to NB-S1-mode operation and is conditional on UE WUS capability indication and UE provision of WUS assistance information.

results.question: Why would the network be prohibited from including the Negotiated WUS assistance information IE during a specific type of attachment procedure?
results.reference: The network is prohibited from including the IE when the UE is attaching for emergency bearer services, as this is an explicit exclusion condition stated in the clause.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.26.27, Negotiated WUS assistance information
results.model_answer: The prohibition applies to an emergency attach. Negotiated WUS assistance is a power-saving/paging-assistance feature intended for normal EPS service operation; it is not negotiated for an attach whose purpose is limited to establishing emergency bearer service. Therefore, even if WUS-related assistance was requested or is otherwise applicable, the MME must not include the Negotiated WUS assistance information IE in the ATTACH ACCEPT for an emergency attach.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2.2 (Attach accept), in the normative rules for inclusion of the Negotiated WUS assistance information IE: the MME shall not include this IE in an ATTACH ACCEPT message during an emergency attach procedure. The associated ATTACH ACCEPT message/IE encoding is specified in clause 9.4.2.2.

results.question: How does the clause define the required support from both the UE and the MME for the network to include the Negotiated WUS assistance information IE?
results.reference: The clause requires that the UE supports WUS assistance and that the MME both supports and accepts the use of WUS assistance. Both conditions must be met.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.26.27, Negotiated WUS assistance information
results.model_answer: The inclusion is gated by bilateral support: the network includes the Negotiated WUS assistance information IE only when the UE has indicated support for WUS assistance information (via its NAS capability indication) and the MME also supports the WUS-assistance feature. Thus, UE support alone is insufficient, and an MME that does not support the feature must not include the IE.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2.4 (ATTACH ACCEPT), with the corresponding TAU-accept rule in clause 5.5.3.2.4. The condition is expressed as support by both the UE and the MME for WUS assistance information before inclusion of the Negotiated WUS assistance information IE.

results.question: What are the functional prerequisites related to network and UE capabilities that mandate the inclusion of the Negotiated WUS assistance information IE?
results.reference: The functional prerequisites are the UE's support for WUS assistance and the MME's support and acceptance of WUS assistance use. The absence of an emergency bearer services attachment is also a prerequisite.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.26.27, Negotiated WUS assistance information
results.model_answer: The IE is mandatory only when both sides support the WUS-assistance feature: (1) the serving network/MME supports WUS assistance information, and (2) the UE has advertised support for WUS assistance information in its UE capability signalling (the relevant Extended UE Network Capability indication). When both conditions hold, the MME shall include the Negotiated WUS assistance information IE in the applicable accept message. If either capability is absent, the IE is not mandated.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.8.1 (ATTACH ACCEPT), conditional-presence rule for the Negotiated WUS assistance information IE; the equivalent conditional rule is also applicable in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message definition. The condition is expressed in terms of network support for WUS assistance information and UE indication of WUS-assistance-information support.

results.question: How does the network's support for PSM influence the inclusion of the T3324 value IE?
results.reference: The network includes the T3324 value IE only if it supports PSM and accepts its use, in addition to the UE having included the IE in the request.
results.model_answer: PSM support is the gate for this IE: when the network supports PSM, the MME includes the T3324 value IE in the applicable accept message to provide the UE’s negotiated Active Time. If PSM is not supported, the network does not provide T3324 as a PSM configuration; consequently PSM is not enabled by that procedure. In a UE-initiated PSM request, this is applied together with the UE’s requested timer parameters.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1 (attach procedure, ATTACH ACCEPT construction) and the corresponding clause 5.5.3 (tracking area updating procedure, TAU ACCEPT construction): the MME shall include the T3324 value IE when the network supports PSM (in the relevant PSM negotiation context).

results.question: Why might a network omit the T3324 value IE even if the UE requested it?
results.reference: The network would omit the T3324 value IE if it does not support PSM or does not accept the use of PSM, even if the UE included the IE in the request.
results.model_answer: T3324 (Active Time) is a Power Saving Mode (PSM) negotiation parameter, not a UE-mandated setting. A UE may request it in ATTACH REQUEST or TAU REQUEST, but the MME/network may decline PSM for that UE or current context (e.g., operator policy, subscription, roaming, local capability/configuration, or service constraints). In that case the network can still accept the attach/TAU while omitting the T3324 value IE. The omission means the UE must treat PSM/Active Time as not granted for that procedure and not run T3324 based on its request.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.4.1.2 (UE-initiated attach procedure, ATTACH ACCEPT handling for PSM). The PSM procedure text specifies that the network includes the T3324 value IE when it accepts the UE's PSM request; if it is absent, the UE treats PSM as not accepted and stops/does not run T3324. The equivalent TAU behavior is specified in clause 5.5.3.2 (UE-initiated tracking area updating procedure, TAU ACCEPT handling).

results.question: What condition must be met for a procedure transaction to be considered inactive?
results.reference: The condition is that no procedure transaction exists for the given procedure transaction identifier, meaning there is no active transaction associated with that identifier.
results.model_answer: A procedure transaction is considered inactive when its associated Procedure Transaction Identity (PTI) has been released (i.e., it is no longer allocated to that transaction).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.3.1, "Procedure transaction identity": the procedure transaction is considered inactive when the PTI associated with the procedure transaction is released.

results.question: What is the main function of the EPS Session Management sublayer as described for the radio interface?
results.reference: The main function of the ESM sublayer is to support EPS bearer context handling in both the UE and the MME.
results.model_answer: The EPS Session Management (ESM) sublayer primarily controls EPS bearer contexts: it provides the NAS procedures to establish, maintain/modify, and release EPS bearers (and associated PDN connectivity) between the UE and the EPS network.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 4.2 (EPS session management), describes the ESM sublayer as providing procedures for the establishment, maintenance and release of EPS bearer contexts, together with PDN-connection handling.

results.question: Under what general condition can ESM procedures be performed, and what is the exception for the first default bearer?
results.reference: Generally, ESM procedures require an established EMM context and initiated secure NAS message exchange. The exception is that the first default EPS bearer context can be activated during the initial attach procedure before these general conditions are fully met.
results.model_answer: In general, ESM procedures are performed only when the UE is in EMM-CONNECTED mode. The exception is the PDN connectivity/default EPS bearer activation associated with the first default EPS bearer context: it may be performed while the UE is in EMM-IDLE mode.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.2.1 (General): ESM procedures are restricted to EMM-CONNECTED mode, with an exception for the procedure concerning the first default EPS bearer context.

results.question: What are the possible outcomes when a UE requests the network to allocate, modify, or release EPS bearer resources?
results.reference: The network can fulfil such a request by activating a new dedicated EPS bearer context, modifying an existing EPS bearer context, or deactivating an EPS bearer context.
results.model_answer: For a UE-initiated bearer-resource request, the network has two normative outcomes: accept it by initiating the corresponding network-initiated EPS bearer-context procedure, or reject it with the applicable ESM reject message and ESM cause. Allocation is accepted through dedicated EPS bearer activation; modification is accepted through EPS bearer-context modification. TS 24.301 does not define a UE "bearer resource release request" message: network release of an EPS bearer is performed by the network-initiated EPS bearer-context deactivation procedure. A UE that wants to release an entire PDN connection uses PDN DISCONNECT REQUEST; the network then deactivates the associated bearer context(s).
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clauses: 3GPP TS 24.301, clauses 6.5 (UE requested bearer resource allocation procedure) and 6.6 (UE requested bearer resource modification procedure): the network either initiates the applicable dedicated-bearer activation/modification procedure or returns BEARER RESOURCE ALLOCATION REJECT / BEARER RESOURCE MODIFICATION REJECT. For release, see clause 6.4.5 (EPS bearer context deactivation procedure) and the PDN disconnect procedure clause; deactivation is network initiated and is acknowledged by DEACTIVATE EPS BEARER CONTEXT ACCEPT.

results.question: Under what conditions must the Voice domain preference and UE's usage setting IE be included in WB-S1 mode according to the clause?
results.reference: It must be included if the UE supports CS fallback and SMS over SGs, OR if the UE is configured for IMS voice but does not support 1xCS fallback.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.29.19, Voice domain preference and UE   's usage setting
results.model_answer: In WB-S1 mode, the UE shall include the Voice domain preference and UE's usage setting IE in the ATTACH REQUEST when it is configured to use either CS fallback (CSFB) or IMS voice over PS sessions. Thus, inclusion is driven by the UE's voice-service configuration; it is not required merely because the UE is in WB-S1 mode. The emergency-attach case is treated separately by the attach-procedure rules.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2.2 (UE-initiated attach procedure / ATTACH REQUEST construction). The WB-S1-specific rule states, in substance, that the UE shall include the Voice domain preference and UE's usage setting IE if it is configured to use CS fallback or IMS voice over PS session(s). Relevant IE semantics are specified in TS 24.301 clause 9.9.3.44.

results.question: How does the UE's support for IMS voice configuration relate to the inclusion of the Voice domain preference and UE's usage setting IE in WB-S1 mode?
results.reference: If the UE is configured to support IMS voice but lacks support for 1xCS fallback, the IE shall be included in WB-S1 mode.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.29.19, Voice domain preference and UE   's usage setting
results.model_answer: In WB-S1 mode, IMS-voice configuration is the trigger for mandatory signalling: a UE configured to support IMS voice over PS session shall include the Voice domain preference and UE's usage setting IE in the ATTACH REQUEST. The condition concerns UE configuration for IMS voice, not whether the UE is currently IMS-registered or has an active IMS voice bearer. The IE conveys the UE's voice-domain preference and voice-centric/data-centric usage setting to the EPS network.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2 (Attach request), which states in substance: if the UE is in WB-S1 mode and is configured to support IMS voice over PS session, the UE shall include the Voice domain preference and UE's usage setting IE in the ATTACH REQUEST. See also TS 24.301 clause 8.2.4 (ATTACH REQUEST) and clause 9.9.3.44 (Voice domain preference and UE's usage setting IE).

results.question: What are the two distinct UE capability scenarios that mandate inclusion of the Voice domain preference and UE's usage setting IE in WB-S1 mode?
results.reference: The two scenarios are: 1) UE supports both CS fallback and SMS over SGs, or 2) UE is configured for IMS voice but does not support 1xCS fallback.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.29.19, Voice domain preference and UE   's usage setting
results.model_answer: In WB-S1 mode, the UE shall include the Voice domain preference and UE's usage setting IE in the ATTACH REQUEST in either of these capability cases: (1) the UE supports IMS voice over PS sessions; or (2) the UE supports CS fallback (CSFB), i.e., fallback to GERAN/UTRAN for circuit-switched voice.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2 (ATTACH REQUEST message transmission): "In WB-S1 mode, the UE shall include the Voice domain preference and UE's usage setting IE ... if the UE supports IMS voice over PS sessions or if the UE supports CS fallback."

results.question: Why would a UE configured for IMS voice need to include the Voice domain preference and UE's usage setting IE in WB-S1 mode?
results.reference: Because when configured for IMS voice, the IE is required if the UE does not support 1xCS fallback, as specified for WB-S1 mode inclusion.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.29.19, Voice domain preference and UE   's usage setting
results.model_answer: Because IMS-voice configuration alone does not tell the MME the UE’s currently provisioned voice-domain policy. In WB-S1 mode, TS 24.301 requires a UE configured to support IMS voice over PS to signal the Voice domain preference and UE’s usage setting so the network can distinguish IMS-PS versus CS voice preference/fallback behavior and whether the UE is voice-centric or data-centric. The MME can then apply the appropriate EPS/CS interworking, CS-fallback and mobility/registration handling. This is a mandatory NAS indication in the stated condition; it is not merely an IMS capability advertisement.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2.2, "ATTACH REQUEST" (release-dependent numbering/text): the UE shall include the Voice domain preference and UE's usage setting IE in an ATTACH REQUEST if the UE is configured to support IMS voice over PS sessions and is operating in WB-S1 mode. Relevant IE definition: TS 24.301 clause 9.9.3.44, "Voice domain preference and UE's usage setting."

results.question: How does a UE capable of both S1 mode and A/Gb or Iu mode manage its registration status when both GMM and EMM are enabled?
results.reference: The UE maintains one common registration for both GMM and EMM that indicates whether the UE is registered for packet services or not.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.1.4, Coordination between EMM and GMM
results.model_answer: The UE maintains GMM and EMM registration status separately and independently. Thus, it can be registered for EPS services (EMM-REGISTERED) while not registered for GPRS/UMTS packet services (GMM-DEREGISTERED), or vice versa. Combined EPS/IMSI attach, tracking-area update, and detach procedures may update both domains together when applicable, but they do not eliminate the separate GMM and EMM state/status management.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 4.2.2 (EMM states; clause numbering/title can vary by release). Its UE-behaviour text for a UE supporting both S1 mode and A/Gb or Iu mode, with both EMM and GMM enabled, requires separate maintenance of the GMM and EMM registration states. GMM procedures/states are specified in 3GPP TS 24.008.

results.question: What are the resulting GMM and EMM substates after a UE successfully performs a GPRS attach or combined GPRS attach procedure in A/Gb or Iu mode?
results.reference: The UE enters substates GMM-REGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE and EMM-REGISTERED.NO-CELL-AVAILABLE, and resets both the attach attempt counter and the GPRS attach attempt counter.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.1.4, Coordination between EMM and GMM
results.model_answer: After successful GPRS attach or combined GPRS attach in A/Gb or Iu mode, the UE enters GMM-REGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE and EMM-DEREGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE. Thus, it is registered for legacy PS-domain GPRS mobility management, but remains deregistered for EPS mobility management.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.2.2 (GPRS attach procedure / successful completion). The normative behavior is that successful GPRS or combined GPRS attach causes entry to GMM-REGISTERED with substate GMM-REGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE, and to EMM-DEREGISTERED with substate EMM-DEREGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE.

results.question: What actions must a UE take during an intersystem change from A/Gb or Iu mode to S1 mode when no PDP context is active, if the UE or MME does not support EMM-REGISTERED without a PDN connection?
results.reference: The UE shall move to state EMM-DEREGISTERED and state GMM-DEREGISTERED and then initiate an attach procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.1.4, Coordination between EMM and GMM
results.model_answer: The UE shall initiate the EPS attach procedure (i.e., send an ATTACH REQUEST), rather than perform a tracking area update based on the intersystem change. Since neither the UE nor the MME supports EMM-REGISTERED without a PDN connection, an EPS registration without PDN connectivity cannot be retained/created; the attach therefore establishes EPS registration with PDN connectivity as applicable.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.3.2.2 (UE initiated tracking area updating procedure): for an intersystem change from A/Gb or Iu mode to S1 mode with no active PDP context, the UE shall initiate the attach procedure if either the UE or the MME does not support EMM-REGISTERED without a PDN connection.

results.question: Under what condition does a UE maintain registration and related periodic update timers in both GMM and EMM after successful completion of certain updating procedures in both S1 mode and A/Gb or Iu mode?
results.reference: The UE shall maintain them if the network has indicated that Idle mode Signalling Reduction (ISR) is activated.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.1.4, Coordination between EMM and GMM
results.model_answer: The UE does this when Idle Mode Signalling Reduction (ISR) is activated. With ISR active, after a successful tracking area updating procedure in S1 mode or routing area updating procedure in A/Gb or Iu mode, the UE retains registration in both EMM and GMM and maintains both periodic-update timers: T3412 (periodic TAU) and T3312 (periodic RAU).
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.3.5, "Idle mode signalling reduction (ISR)" (clause numbering may vary by release). The ISR UE-behaviour requirement states that, when ISR is activated, the UE maintains registration with both the MME and SGSN and maintains the periodic TAU and RAU timers following successful updating in S1 or A/Gb/Iu mode.

results.question: How does the NBIFOM container relate to other 3GPP specifications?
results.reference: The information transferred by the NBIFOM container is associated with network-based IP flow mobility as defined in 3GPP TS 24.161.
results.model_answer: The NBIFOM container is a NAS transport container defined as an information element in TS 24.301, but its NBIFOM-specific payload semantics and coding are specified by TS 24.302. Thus, TS 24.301 provides the EPS NAS message/IE framework and transport, while TS 24.302 defines the Network-Based IP Flow Mobility (NBIFOM) content carried in that container. The underlying service architecture is specified at stage 2 in TS 23.261, with EPC/non-3GPP interworking context in TS 23.402.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.4, under the "NBIFOM container" IE definition (subclause number is release-dependent). The normative statement is effectively: "The NBIFOM container is specified in 3GPP TS 24.302."

results.question: What type of information does the NBIFOM container element carry?
results.reference: It carries information associated with network-based IP flow mobility.
results.model_answer: The NBIFOM container IE carries Network-Based IP Flow Mobility (NBIFOM) information—i.e., information used to support network-controlled IP-flow routing/mobility between 3GPP and WLAN accesses.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9, "NBIFOM container". Its normative purpose statement is that the NBIFOM container information element is used to carry NBIFOM information (with NBIFOM specified in TS 24.302).

results.question: Why is the NBIFOM container information element included in TS 24.301?
results.reference: To enable the transfer of network-based IP flow mobility information as specified in TS 24.161.
results.model_answer: The NBIFOM container IE is included to let EPS NAS transport NBIFOM-specific control information between the UE and the NBIFOM network function/PDN-GW side. NBIFOM supports network-controlled steering or movement of individual IP flows between 3GPP and non-3GPP accesses while retaining the applicable PDN connectivity. The IE is a container so intermediate NAS entities need not interpret the NBIFOM payload; they convey it as part of the relevant ESM procedure. It therefore provides the NAS carriage needed for NBIFOM capability/mode and procedure-related signalling, rather than itself defining IP-flow routing decisions.
results.evidence: {'most_likely_clause': '3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.4, "NBIFOM container" IE definition (subclause numbering can vary by release).', 'reason': 'The IE definition specifies a dedicated NAS container for carrying NBIFOM information. The associated NBIFOM procedure/behaviour clauses in TS 24.301 explain its use in ESM signalling; the NBIFOM-specific payload/protocol is specified by the NBIFOM stage-3 specification rather than being interpreted generically by NAS.'}

results.question: How is the scenario where a UE receives EMM cause #78 from a non-satellite E-UTRA cell classified, and what determines the UE's behavior in this case?
results.reference: This scenario is considered an abnormal case. The specific behavior of the UE in this abnormal case is defined in clause 5.5.1.2.6 of the specification.
results.gold_evidence: This cause value received from a non-satellite E-UTRA cell is considered as an abnormal case and the behaviour of the UE is specified in clause 5.5.1.2.6
results.model_answer: EMM cause #78 denotes "S1 mode not allowed." If it is received from a non-satellite E-UTRA cell, it is handled as an S1-mode restriction for that cell/access, not as a satellite-specific condition. The UE’s consequent action is determined by the reject procedure in which the cause is received (e.g. attach or tracking-area update) and by whether the UE can use/select an alternative access mode, notably N1 mode/5GS where applicable.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.4 (UE handling of ATTACH REJECT) and the corresponding TAU-reject handling in clause 5.5.3.2.7, read with the EMM-cause-value definition in clause 9.9.3.9. These provisions define cause #78 as "S1 mode not allowed" and prescribe reject-procedure-dependent UE handling.

results.question: When shall a UE that supports CE mode B and operates in WB-S1 mode not using satellite E-UTRAN access NOT apply the NAS timer values for WB-S1/CE mode?
results.reference: The UE shall not apply the NAS timer values for WB-S1/CE mode before receiving an indication from the network that the use of enhanced coverage is not restricted as described in the clause.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.8.1, UE not using satellite E-UTRAN access
results.model_answer: Only when the UE is using satellite E-UTRAN access. The WB-S1/CE-mode NAS-timer requirement is explicitly qualified as applying except for satellite E-UTRAN access. Therefore, a CE mode B-capable UE operating in WB-S1 mode and not using satellite E-UTRAN access shall apply the WB-S1/CE-mode NAS timer values; it has no exemption on those facts alone.
results.evidence: Likely TS 24.301 timers-and-constants clause: "Except for a UE using satellite E-UTRAN access, a UE that supports CE mode B and operates in WB-S1 mode shall apply the NAS timer values for WB-S1/CE mode ..." The stated exception is satellite E-UTRAN access.

results.question: How is the support of CE mode B by a UE indicated to the MME, and what action does the MME take with this information?
results.reference: The support of CE mode B by a UE is indicated to the MME by lower layers and shall be stored by the MME.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.8.1, UE not using satellite E-UTRAN access
results.model_answer: The UE indicates CE mode B capability by setting the CE mode B support indication in the UE network capability IE (carried in NAS registration-management requests, e.g. ATTACH REQUEST and, when applicable, TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST). The MME stores this UE capability and uses it for paging: when paging the UE, it provides the CE mode B support indication to E-UTRAN so that the eNB can apply CE mode B paging/procedures where appropriate.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2 (ATTACH REQUEST transmission/message contents), read with clause 9.9.3.34 (UE network capability IE). These specify the UE network-capability indication, including CE mode B support; the associated NAS procedure text requires the MME to retain/use the indication for paging towards E-UTRAN.

results.question: What actions does a UE take upon the first expiry of timer T3493 during the Remote UE Report procedure?
