results.reference: The UE resends the REMOTE UE REPORT message and resets and restarts timer T3493.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.6.3.5, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: On the first expiry of T3493, the UE retransmits the REMOTE UE REPORT message and restarts T3493. The procedure is therefore retried once; it is not aborted on the first expiry.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause titled "Remote UE report procedure", subclause describing "Expiry of timer T3493": on the first expiry, the UE retransmits the REMOTE UE REPORT message and restarts T3493.

results.question: How many times can timer T3493 expire before the UE aborts the Remote UE Report procedure?
results.reference: The UE aborts the procedure on the third expiry of timer T3493.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.6.3.5, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: Five expiries. The UE aborts the Remote UE Report procedure on the fifth expiry of T3493; therefore, no retransmission/restart is performed after that expiry.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 11.2.2 (Timer T3493): the T3493 expiry handling for the Remote UE Report procedure specifies aborting the procedure after the fifth expiry of T3493.

results.question: What happens after the UE aborts the Remote UE Report procedure due to timer T3493 expiry?
results.reference: The UE releases any resources for this procedure, and the procedure for the remote UE(s) can be restarted, with the restart method left to UE implementation.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.6.3.5, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: On T3493 expiry, the UE aborts the Remote UE Report procedure and treats the outstanding REMOTE UE REPORT as unsuccessful. The specification does not mandate another retransmission of that report as part of the T3493-expiry handling; the UE resumes normal EMM operation (subject to any other ongoing NAS procedure).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.13.4.2 (Remote UE report procedure), together with the T3493 definition/expiry action in clause 10.2: T3493 is associated with the Remote UE Report procedure and, on expiry, the UE aborts that procedure.

results.question: Describe the complete retransmission behavior of the REMOTE UE REPORT message upon successive expiries of timer T3493.
results.reference: On the first expiry, the UE resends the message and restarts T3493. This is repeated on the second expiry. On the third expiry, the UE aborts the procedure and releases resources.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.6.3.5, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: T3493 is started after sending a REMOTE UE REPORT. If no successful procedure completion occurs before expiry, the UE retransmits the same REMOTE UE REPORT and restarts T3493 on each of the first four expiries. Thus, expiry #1, #2, #3, and #4 each cause one retransmission and a timer restart. On expiry #5, the UE does not send another REMOTE UE REPORT; it stops/refrains from restarting T3493 and aborts the remote-UE-report procedure. This is four retransmissions in addition to the original transmission.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.10.3.3 (Remote UE report procedure; clause numbering can vary by release), together with the T3493 entry in the NAS timer definitions. The procedure specifies retransmission and restart of T3493, repeated four times, and abortion of the procedure on the fifth expiry of T3493.

results.question: Under what specific conditions is the NonceUE information element included by the UE?
results.reference: The UE includes the NonceUE IE when it performs an inter-system change from A/Gb mode or Iu mode to S1 mode while in idle mode, and its Temporary Identity used in Next update (TIN) is set to "P-TMSI".
results.model_answer: The UE includes the NonceUE IE only in a SECURITY MODE COMPLETE message, and only when the received SECURITY MODE COMMAND contained the NonceMME IE. This presupposes that the UE accepts the SECURITY MODE COMMAND and sends SECURITY MODE COMPLETE; if it rejects the command, it sends SECURITY MODE REJECT instead.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.4.3.2 (security mode control procedure initiated by the network): if the SECURITY MODE COMMAND includes the NonceMME IE, the UE shall include the NonceUE IE in the SECURITY MODE COMPLETE message.

results.question: How does the UE's operational state and TIN setting determine the inclusion of the NonceUE information element?
results.reference: The UE includes the NonceUE IE only when it is executing an idle mode inter-system change from either A/Gb or Iu mode to S1 mode, and its TIN parameter is configured to the value "P-TMSI".
results.model_answer: NonceUE is included only when the UE is carrying a P-TMSI-based inter-system identity context. The EMM state selects the NAS procedure: an EMM-DEREGISTERED UE includes NonceUE in an ATTACH REQUEST when its TIN is set to "P-TMSI"; an EMM-REGISTERED UE includes it in a TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST when its TIN is set to "P-TMSI". A TIN set to "GUTI" or "IMSI" does not by itself trigger NonceUE inclusion. The purpose is to support use/mapping of the pre-EPS security context associated with the P-TMSI context.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clauses 5.5.1.2.2 (initiation of attach) and 5.5.3.2.2 (initiation of tracking area updating): the UE includes the NonceUE IE in the respective ATTACH REQUEST or TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST when the TIN is set to "P-TMSI". The applicable procedure follows the UE's EMM state: attach from EMM-DEREGISTERED and TAU from EMM-REGISTERED.

results.question: In which inter-system mobility scenario and with what identity context is the NonceUE information element generated?
results.reference: The NonceUE IE is generated during an idle mode inter-system change where the UE moves from either the A/Gb mode or the Iu mode to the S1 mode, provided the UE's Temporary Identity used in Next update (TIN) is set to "P-TMSI".
results.model_answer: NonceUE is generated by the UE for an inter-system change from GERAN or UTRAN to E-UTRAN when the UE has a valid mapped EPS security context. The context is the EPS security context mapped from the 2G/3G security context (rather than a newly established native EPS context), identified/selected using the associated old EPS identity/security-context information, e.g. old GUTI and mapped NAS key-set context. It is carried in the relevant TAU REQUEST procedure.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, EMM tracking-area-update procedure and NonceUE IE specification: the UE generates/includes NonceUE when it has a valid mapped EPS security context and performs an inter-system change from GERAN/UTRAN to E-UTRAN. The nonce supports the security-context/key handling associated with that mapped context.

results.question: What is the significance of the BEARER CONTEXT ACTIVE PENDING state in the EPS bearer context activation procedure?
results.reference: It indicates that the network has initiated an EPS bearer context activation procedure towards the UE, meaning the activation process has been started by the network but is not yet completed.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.1.3.3.2, BEARER CONTEXT ACTIVE PENDING
results.model_answer: BEARER CONTEXT ACTIVE PENDING is the transitional ESM state meaning that activation of a particular EPS bearer context has been initiated but is not yet completed. It prevents the context from being treated as fully active while the activation request/accept exchange and associated access-stratum bearer setup are outstanding. On successful completion the context moves to BEARER CONTEXT ACTIVE; on rejection, timeout, or activation failure it is released/returned to an inactive state. At the network side, it notably represents an activation request sent for which the corresponding acceptance is still awaited; at the UE side it covers processing of the received activation request and coordination with lower layers before completion.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.4.1 (EPS/default bearer context activation procedure) and clause 6.4.2 (dedicated EPS bearer context activation procedure), in the state-handling text specifying entry into BEARER CONTEXT ACTIVE PENDING when bearer-context activation is initiated and transition to BEARER CONTEXT ACTIVE after successful completion. The ESM bearer-context state model in clause 5.2 also provides the contextual definition of the per-bearer ESM states.

results.question: How does the BEARER CONTEXT ACTIVE PENDING state relate to the entity initiating the bearer activation?
results.reference: The state specifically denotes that the network is the entity that has initiated the EPS bearer context activation procedure directed at the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.1.3.3.2, BEARER CONTEXT ACTIVE PENDING
results.model_answer: BEARER CONTEXT ACTIVE PENDING denotes that the UE has initiated a dedicated-bearer resource allocation request, but the actual dedicated EPS bearer activation is still to be initiated by the network. Thus, it is a UE-requested resource-allocation situation with a network-initiated bearer activation procedure pending.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.4.1.3 (BEARER CONTEXT ACTIVE PENDING state): the state is entered following UE initiation of bearer resource allocation for a dedicated EPS bearer context and indicates that the UE is waiting for the network to initiate the dedicated bearer activation procedure.

results.question: How does the network initiate the ESM information request procedure?
results.reference: The network initiates the procedure by sending an ESM INFORMATION REQUEST message to the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.6.1.2, ESM information request procedure
results.model_answer: The MME/network initiates the procedure by sending an ESM INFORMATION REQUEST message to the UE (as ESM NAS signalling), normally in association with a UE-initiated PDN connectivity procedure when additional ESM information—such as the APN and/or protocol configuration options—is needed. The UE then returns an ESM INFORMATION RESPONSE message using the corresponding procedure transaction identity.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.5.1.2 ("ESM information request procedure initiation"): the network initiates the ESM information request procedure by sending an ESM INFORMATION REQUEST message to the UE.

results.question: Under what specific conditions must the Header compression configuration IE be included in a message according to clause 8.3.18.12?
results.reference: The IE must be included when the network wants to re-negotiate header compression for an EPS bearer context, and only if both the UE and the network support Control plane CIoT EPS optimization and header compression.
results.model_answer: The IE is mandatory only when header compression has been negotiated between the network and the UE. Under that condition, it shall be included in an ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST, ACTIVATE DEDICATED EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST, or MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message. The requirement is tied to negotiated header compression, not merely to UE capability to support it.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 8.3.18.12: "The Header compression configuration IE shall be included in the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message, ACTIVATE DEDICATED EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message, and MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message if the network has negotiated header compression with the UE."

results.question: What are the two distinct capabilities that both the UE and network must possess for the Header compression configuration IE to be included for re-negotiation?
results.reference: Both must support Control plane CIoT EPS optimization and must also support header compression.
results.model_answer: Both ends must support (1) header compression itself and (2) re-negotiation of the header-compression configuration. Support for only the compression function is insufficient; UE and network must also both support changing/renegotiating its configuration.
results.evidence: TS 24.301, the Header compression configuration IE presence condition in the Activate dedicated EPS bearer context request message content: the IE is included when header-compression configuration is to be re-negotiated and both the UE and the network support header compression and re-negotiation of header-compression configuration.

results.question: Why would a UE transition to the EMM-DEREGISTERED state with substate ATTEMPTING-TO-ATTACH?
results.reference: This occurs when the UE initiates an attach procedure but the request is not accepted by the network, causing the UE to remain detached while it may still be attempting to attach based on implementation-specific procedures.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.1.3.2.3, Substates of state EMM-DEREGISTERED
results.model_answer: A UE enters EMM-DEREGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-TO-ATTACH when it initiates an EPS attach procedure. This means the UE has no current valid EPS registration and is actively attempting to establish one; it is not, by itself, an indication of an attach failure. Typical triggers are power-on/initial registration after selecting a suitable cell, regaining service while deregistered, a local or network-initiated detach, or retrying attachment after a previous attach attempt did not establish EPS registration. The UE remains in this substate while awaiting ATTACH ACCEPT/REJECT and during applicable attach retransmission handling (e.g. T3410).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.3.2 (Attach procedure; in some releases clause 5.3.2.1, General): upon initiation of the attach procedure, the UE shall enter EMM-DEREGISTERED state with EMM substate ATTEMPTING-TO-ATTACH.

results.question: What types of protocol data can be transmitted using the protocol configuration options IE described in clause 8.3.16.2?
results.reference: It can transmit data such as configuration parameters, error codes, or messages/events.
results.model_answer: It can carry PPP protocol data and 3GPP-specific protocol data (including one or more protocol-configuration option containers).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 8.3.16.2 (Protocol configuration options) specifies that the protocol configuration options IE can be used to transfer PPP protocol data and 3GPP-specific protocol data.

results.question: What is the purpose of referencing 3GPP TS 24.008 clause 10.5.4.32 in the Supported codec list definition?
results.reference: The reference specifies the detailed format, encoding rules, and structure of the Supported codec list information element, which is defined in the core NAS specifications rather than being duplicated in TS 24.301.
results.model_answer: The reference imports the existing 24.008 definition of the Supported Codec List IE into EPS NAS. Its purpose is to ensure that the UE and network use the same IE format, codec identifiers, bitmap semantics, and length/coding rules already defined for 2G/3G NAS, rather than creating an LTE-specific duplicate definition. In 24.301 procedures such as Attach and Tracking Area Update, this lets the UE convey its supported speech codecs consistently, notably for interworking/CS-fallback-related handling.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.3.34 (Supported codec list), which normatively states that the Supported codec list IE is coded as specified in 3GPP TS 24.008 clause 10.5.4.32. TS 24.008 clause 10.5.4.32 is therefore the normative source for the IE's value-part coding and codec-list interpretation.

results.question: How does the network utilize the Supported codec list information provided by the UE?
results.reference: The network uses this information to determine compatible codecs for voice and multimedia sessions, ensuring interoperability and optimal resource allocation during call setup and bearer establishment.
results.model_answer: The MME stores the UE's Supported codec list and, when CS-domain interworking is applicable (for example, combined EPS/IMSI attach with an SGs association), conveys it to the MSC/VLR over SGs. The MSC/VLR can then use the UE's advertised CS speech-codec capabilities when handling CS voice service, including CS fallback-related call handling and codec selection in GERAN/UTRAN. The IE does not itself perform VoLTE/IMS codec negotiation; IMS media codecs are negotiated separately, typically using SDP.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2.2 (network-side handling of ATTACH REQUEST/combined attach), read with the "Supported codec list" IE definition in clause 9.9.2. The network-side procedure requires the MME to retain the UE-provided codec information and, where an SGs association/CS-domain registration is performed, provide it to the MSC/VLR. The IE definition identifies it as UE codec-capability information for CS speech-service use.

results.question: What is the primary purpose of the ESM message container information element as defined in the clause?
results.reference: The primary purpose is to enable the piggybacked transfer of a single ESM message within an EMM message.
results.model_answer: The ESM message container IE encapsulates and transports a complete ESM message within an EMM NAS message, allowing EMM and ESM procedures to be carried together (for example, PDN connectivity and bearer-context signalling during attach).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.4.12, "ESM message container": the IE is used to encapsulate an ESM message transferred between the UE and the MME.

results.question: How must the ESM message included within the ESM message container information element be coded?
results.reference: It must be coded as specified in clause 8.3, meaning without a NAS security header.
results.model_answer: The embedded ESM message shall be coded as an ESM message in accordance with TS 24.301 clause 9.3 (i.e., using the normal ESM message coding/format), and carried as the contents of the ESM message container IE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.4 (ESM message container): the ESM message included in the ESM message container information element shall be coded as specified in clause 9.3.

results.question: According to the clause, what type of information element is the ESM message container classified as?
results.reference: It is classified as a type 6 information element.
results.model_answer: The ESM message container is classified as a Type 6 information element.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.4 ("ESM message container"): "The ESM message container is a type 6 information element."

results.question: Which figures and tables specify the coding structure for the ESM message container information element?
results.reference: The coding is shown in figure 9.9.3.15.1 and table 9.9.3.15.1.
results.model_answer: The coding structure of the ESM message container IE is specified by Figure 9.9.3.15.1, “ESM message container information element”, and Table 9.9.3.15.1, “ESM message container information element”, in 3GPP TS 24.301 clause 9.9.3.15.
results.evidence: TS 24.301, clause 9.9.3.15, introduces the ESM message container IE and refers to Figure 9.9.3.15.1 and Table 9.9.3.15.1 for its encoded layout and field definitions.

results.question: Under what condition is timer T3412 deactivated, and what is the resulting UE behavior regarding periodic tracking area updates?
results.reference: Timer T3412 is deactivated if the received timer value in an ATTACH ACCEPT or TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message indicates deactivation or is zero. When deactivated, the UE shall not perform the periodic tracking area updating procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.5, Handling of the periodic tracking area update timer and mobile reachable timer (S1 mode only)
results.model_answer: T3412 is deactivated when the UE receives a periodic TAU timer value indicating “timer deactivated” (e.g., in an ATTACH ACCEPT or TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT). The UE then does not initiate periodic tracking area updates on T3412 expiry, because no periodic-TAU timer is running. TAUs may still be initiated for other applicable triggers, such as mobility/TA change or explicit network requirements.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.3.2 (Periodic updating): the periodic TAU timer value can indicate that the timer is deactivated; in that case the UE deactivates T3412 and does not perform periodic tracking area updating.

results.question: How does the UE's state transition affect the operation of timer T3412?
results.reference: Timer T3412 is reset and started with its initial value when the UE changes from EMM-CONNECTED to EMM-IDLE mode. It is stopped when the UE enters EMM-CONNECTED mode or the EMM-DEREGISTERED state.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.5, Handling of the periodic tracking area update timer and mobile reachable timer (S1 mode only)
results.model_answer: T3412 is tied to the EMM registration state. The UE starts (or keeps running) T3412 when it enters EMM-REGISTERED, and stops it when it leaves EMM-REGISTERED, e.g. on transition to EMM-DEREGISTERED. Expiry of a running T3412 causes the UE to perform periodic tracking area updating, subject to the applicable NAS procedure conditions. An ECM-IDLE/ECM-CONNECTED change alone does not constitute leaving EMM-REGISTERED and therefore is not, by itself, the EMM-state stop condition.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 11.2.2, Timer T3412 (periodic tracking area updating timer): T3412 is started when the UE enters EMM-REGISTERED and stopped when the UE leaves EMM-REGISTERED; expiry is associated with periodic tracking area updating. See also clause 5.2 for EMM state behavior.

results.question: What specific action must the UE take if attached for emergency bearer services and timer T3412 expires?
results.reference: If the UE is attached for emergency bearer services and timer T3412 expires, the UE shall not initiate a periodic tracking area updating procedure but shall instead locally detach from the network.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.5, Handling of the periodic tracking area update timer and mobile reachable timer (S1 mode only)
results.model_answer: The UE shall initiate a tracking area updating (TAU) procedure, using the periodic updating cause/update type, when T3412 expires. This applies even when the UE is attached only for emergency bearer services.
results.evidence: Most likely clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.3.2 (Initiation of the tracking area updating procedure). It specifies that a UE attached for emergency bearer services shall initiate the TAU procedure on expiry of timer T3412 (the periodic TAU timer).

results.question: What capability regarding the Ethernet PDN type can a UE possess according to the clause?
results.reference: A UE may support the Ethernet PDN type.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.3.12, Handling of Ethernet PDN type
results.model_answer: A UE can be capable of supporting the Ethernet PDN type and, when establishing a PDN connection, can request PDN type Ethernet.
results.evidence: Most likely: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.10.2.1 (initiation of PDN connectivity procedure), together with clause 9.9.3.12 (PDN type information element), which defines Ethernet as a PDN type that may be requested/indicated by a UE supporting it.

results.question: What does the clause state about the possibility of a UE handling Ethernet PDN connections?
results.reference: The clause indicates that support for the Ethernet PDN type by a UE is optional, as it states the UE may support it.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.3.12, Handling of Ethernet PDN type
results.model_answer: The clause permits a UE to request and handle a PDN connection whose PDN type is Ethernet. This is an optional capability: Ethernet PDN connectivity is applicable when supported by the UE and accepted/provisioned by the EPS network; it is not implied to be mandatory for every UE.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.5.1.1 (PDN connectivity procedure — general), which specifies that a UE may request PDN connectivity with PDN type IPv4, IPv6, IPv4v6, non-IP, or Ethernet. Thus, Ethernet is a permitted PDN type for a UE PDN connection.

results.question: According to the clause, what is the nature of a network's support for the Ethernet PDN type?
results.reference: The support is not mandatory for a network; the clause specifies that a network may support this PDN type.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.3.12, Handling of Ethernet PDN type
results.model_answer: Support for the Ethernet PDN type is optional in the network (and also optional in the UE); it is not a mandatory EPS PDN-type capability.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.5.1.1 (PDN connectivity procedure — General): the clause states that support of the Ethernet PDN type is optional for the UE and the network.

results.question: Under what specific ESM cause value conditions may the network include the Re-attempt indicator IE when it is also including the Back-off timer value IE?
results.reference: The network may include the Re-attempt indicator IE when it includes the Back-off timer value IE only if the ESM cause value is not #26 'insufficient resources'.
results.model_answer: The network may include the Re-attempt indicator IE only when the PDN CONNECTIVITY REJECT carries a Back-off timer value IE and the ESM cause is either #8 "operator determined barring" or #26 "insufficient resources".
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.4.1 (PDN connectivity procedure / PDN CONNECTIVITY REJECT): the network may include the Re-attempt indicator IE if the Back-off timer value IE is included and the ESM cause value is #8 (operator determined barring) or #26 (insufficient resources).

results.question: For which ESM cause values related to PDN type compatibility may the network include the Re-attempt indicator IE?
results.reference: The network may include the IE for ESM cause values #28 'unknown PDN type', #50 'PDN type IPv4 only allowed', #51 'PDN type IPv6 only allowed', #57 'PDN type IPv4v6 only allowed', #58 'PDN type non IP only allowed', and #61 'PDN type Ethernet only allowed'.
results.model_answer: The network may include the Re-attempt indicator IE for ESM causes: #50 "PDN type IPv4 only allowed", #51 "PDN type IPv6 only allowed", and #52 "single address bearers only allowed".
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.5.1.3 (PDN CONNECTIVITY REJECT): when the ESM cause is #50, #51, or #52, the network may include the Re-attempt indicator IE in the PDN CONNECTIVITY REJECT message.

results.question: How does the allowance for including the Re-attempt indicator IE differ when the ESM cause is #66 versus when the network includes a Back-off timer?
results.reference: For cause #66 'requested APN not supported in current RAT and PLMN combination', the network may include the IE directly. When including a Back-off timer, the network may include the IE only if the ESM cause is not #26 'insufficient resources'.
results.model_answer: For a PDN CONNECTIVITY REJECT with ESM cause #66 (“requested APN not supported in current RAT and PLMN combination”), the network may include the Re-attempt indicator IE. In contrast, if the network includes a Back-off timer IE, it shall not include the Re-attempt indicator IE. Thus, #66 permits the indicator, whereas presence of Back-off timer prohibits it.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 8.3.2 (PDN CONNECTIVITY REJECT): “If the ESM cause is set to #66 ‘requested APN not supported in current RAT and PLMN combination’, the network may include the Re-attempt indicator IE.” The same clause states: “The network shall not include the Re-attempt indicator IE if the Back-off timer IE is included.”

results.question: Under what condition must the Device properties IE be included in a NAS message according to clause 8.2.4.14?
results.reference: The Device properties IE must be included when the UE is configured for NAS signalling low priority.
results.model_answer: The UE must include the Device properties IE when it is configured for low priority. This IE conveys the low-priority indication to the network.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 8.2.4.14 (Device properties): the IE shall be included by the UE in the applicable NAS request message if the UE is configured for low priority.

results.question: What UE configuration triggers the mandatory inclusion of the Device properties information element?
results.reference: The mandatory inclusion is triggered when the UE is configured for NAS signalling low priority.
results.model_answer: The UE shall include the Device properties IE when it is configured for low priority (i.e., low-priority UE operation as defined by TS 23.401). This applies to NAS Attach Request and Tracking Area Update Request procedures where the IE is conditionally present.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2 (Attach request): "If the UE is configured for low priority ... the UE shall include the Device properties IE in the ATTACH REQUEST message." The corresponding TAU procedure requirements in clause 5.5.3.2 also require inclusion when the UE is configured for low priority.

results.question: Based on clause 8.2.4.14, when is the inclusion of the Device properties IE not optional for the UE?
results.reference: Its inclusion is not optional and becomes mandatory when the UE is configured for NAS signalling low priority.
results.model_answer: The UE's inclusion of the Device properties IE is mandatory (not optional) when the UE is configured for NAS signalling low priority. In that case, the UE shall include the IE in the applicable EMM request message(s), rather than relying on its otherwise optional presence.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 8.2.4.14 (Device properties): the UE shall include the Device properties IE when it is configured for NAS signalling low priority. The normative "shall include" condition makes inclusion mandatory for that UE state.

results.question: In which specific emergency-related scenarios must a UE configured for NAS signalling low priority explicitly set the low priority indicator to 'MS is not configured for NAS signalling low priority'?
results.reference: The UE must set the indicator to 'not configured' when: 1) performing an attach for emergency bearer services; 2) it has an established emergency PDN connection and is performing EPS mobility management procedures or establishing another emergency PDN connection; 3) performing a service request procedure for a CS fallback or 1xCS fallback emergency call.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.2A, Handling of NAS signalling low priority indication
results.model_answer: A UE configured for NAS signalling low priority shall override its normal setting and encode the low priority indicator as "MS is not configured for NAS signalling low priority" when it is: (1) performing an emergency attach; (2) performing a tracking area updating procedure for emergency bearer services; (3) performing a service request procedure for emergency bearer services; or (4) sending an extended service request for emergency services fallback. The override prevents emergency access from being treated as low-priority NAS signalling.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, UE procedure rules for ATTACH REQUEST, TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST, SERVICE REQUEST and EXTENDED SERVICE REQUEST (clauses 5.5.1, 5.5.3 and 5.6.1, together with the Low priority indicator IE definition in clause 9.9.3). These rules state that a UE configured for NAS signalling low priority uses the "not configured" value for the specified emergency-related procedures.

results.question: How does the network potentially utilize the NAS signalling low priority indication provided by the UE, and what specific action does the MME take if this indication is included in a PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST message?
results.reference: The network may use the indication for NAS level mobility management congestion control and APN based congestion control. If received in a PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST, the MME stores the NAS signalling low priority indication within the default EPS bearer context activated due to that procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.2A, Handling of NAS signalling low priority indication
results.model_answer: The indication tells the network that the UE regards the NAS signalling as low priority. The network may use it for lower-priority handling, for example to preferentially defer, throttle, or reject such signalling during congestion/overload; it does not itself mandate rejection or alter bearer QoS. If a PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST contains the indication, the MME shall forward/include the low-priority indication in the CREATE SESSION REQUEST sent to the Serving GW.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.5.1.2 (UE-requested PDN connectivity procedure): when the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST includes the low priority indication, the MME includes/forwards it in the CREATE SESSION REQUEST towards the S-GW. TS 24.301 clause 9.9.2.10 (Device properties IE) defines the low-priority indicator (LPR) used to signal NAS-signalling low priority.

results.question: Apart from emergency and dual-priority scenarios, what are the other general conditions where a UE configured for NAS signalling low priority must override its configuration and set the low priority indicator to 'MS is not configured for NAS signalling low priority'?
results.reference: The UE must also set the indicator to 'not configured' when: 1) it is a UE configured to use AC11-15 in the selected PLMN; or 2) it is responding to paging.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.2A, Handling of NAS signalling low priority indication
results.model_answer: Other than emergency handling and the explicit dual-priority rules, the low-priority indication is overridden for NAS procedures that also require non-EPS/CS-domain handling: (1) a combined EPS/IMSI attach, (2) a combined tracking-area update (TAU) with IMSI attach, and (3) a Service Request associated with CS fallback. In those cases the UE sets the NAS signalling low priority indicator to "MS is not configured for NAS signalling low priority", even if it is otherwise configured as a low-priority NAS-signalling UE.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, the UE-side rules in the Attach procedure (clause 5.3.2), TAU procedure (clause 5.5.3), and Service Request procedure (clause 5.6.1). These procedure clauses specify the value of the NAS signalling low priority indicator and contain the exceptions for emergency operation, dual-priority operation, and combined/CS-fallback-related procedures.

results.question: What must the network include when modifying the EPS QoS of an EPS bearer context?
results.reference: The network must include the modified EPS QoS assigned to the EPS bearer context.
results.model_answer: When modifying the EPS QoS of an EPS bearer context, the network shall include the EPS QoS information element (IE) in the MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.4.2.2 (network-initiated EPS bearer context modification procedure): if the network modifies the EPS QoS parameters of an EPS bearer context, it shall include the EPS QoS IE in the MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message.

results.question: How does the network proceed when the EPS QoS of an EPS bearer context is modified?
results.reference: It includes the modified EPS QoS that has been assigned to that EPS bearer context.
results.model_answer: When the network changes the EPS QoS of an existing EPS bearer context, it initiates the network-initiated bearer context modification procedure. It sends a MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST for the affected bearer, including the modified EPS QoS parameters. The UE applies the accepted modification and returns MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT ACCEPT; if it cannot accept the requested modification, it returns MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REJECT with an ESM cause.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.4.2 (Bearer context modification procedure), in particular the network-initiated procedure: the network initiates bearer context modification by sending MODIFY EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST to modify EPS bearer-context parameters, including EPS QoS.

results.question: How does the network's acceptance of a specific PDN type relate to the inclusion of the Header compression configuration IE?
results.reference: The network's acceptance of an IP PDN type is one of the two mandatory conditions that must be satisfied for the network to include the Header compression configuration IE in the procedure.
results.model_answer: For an accepted IPv4v6 PDN connection, the network includes the Header compression configuration IE in the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST when header compression has been requested/negotiated. The IE conveys the network-selected header-compression configuration for the accepted PDN connection; acceptance of the PDN connection alone does not imply header compression unless the applicable header-compression condition is met.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.5.1.2 (PDN connectivity procedure accepted by the network), together with the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST message rules in clause 6.5.2 and the Header compression configuration IE definition in clause 9.9.24. The relevant rule is that, when the network accepts an IPv4v6 PDN type, it includes the Header compression configuration IE in the default-bearer activation message when the UE requested header compression and the network accepts/configures it.

results.question: What role does the selection of control plane CIoT EPS optimization play in the network's decision to include the Header compression configuration IE?
results.reference: The selection of control plane CIoT EPS optimization is a necessary condition, which together with the acceptance of an IP PDN type, triggers the network to include the Header compression configuration IE.
results.model_answer: Selection of control plane CIoT EPS optimization is the gating condition for use of NAS/control-plane header compression on the PDN connection. When the network selects that optimization and decides to apply header compression, it includes the Header compression configuration IE in the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST to provide the UE with the compression configuration. If control plane CIoT EPS optimization is not selected, this IE is not applicable and is not included for that purpose.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.5.1.2 (UE-initiated PDN connectivity procedure), in the MME behavior for selection of control plane CIoT EPS optimization and construction of the ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST. The associated message specification/table for ACTIVATE DEFAULT EPS BEARER CONTEXT REQUEST identifies Header compression configuration as conditionally present in relation to control plane CIoT EPS optimization/header-compression use.

results.question: How does the MME handle a NAS signalling message that is received without integrity protection after the secure exchange of NAS messages has been established?
results.reference: The NAS in the MME shall discard this message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.4.4.3, Integrity checking of NAS signalling messages in the MME
results.model_answer: The MME shall discard the NAS signalling message and shall not process it as a valid NAS procedure message. Once a secure NAS exchange/EPS NAS security context is established, an otherwise plain (non-integrity-protected) NAS message is unacceptable unless it is an explicitly specified exception; it must not be used to change EMM/ESM state or trigger the requested procedure.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 4.4.4 (NAS security), particularly the integrity-protection handling rules in clause 4.4.4.2: after secure NAS message exchange has been established, a received NAS signalling message without integrity protection shall be discarded (subject only to explicitly defined exceptions).

results.question: Under what condition regarding emergency services might the MME skip the authentication procedure when an integrity check fails?
results.reference: When the UE has a PDN connection for emergency bearer services or RLOS and the integrity check fails, the MME may skip the authentication procedure even if no EPS security context is available and proceed directly to the security mode control procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.4.4.3, Integrity checking of NAS signalling messages in the MME
results.model_answer: The MME may skip authentication after an integrity-check failure if the UE is requesting emergency services and the MME is configured to permit emergency bearer services without authentication.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.4.2.3 (authentication procedure initiation): authentication may be omitted for an emergency-services request when the MME is configured not to authenticate UEs for emergency services. The integrity-check-failure handling does not prevent this emergency-service exception.

results.question: Under what conditions must a UE include the UE additional security capability IE according to the specified clause?
results.reference: The UE must include this IE if it supports dual connectivity with NR or if it supports N1 mode.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.4.21, UE additional security capability
results.model_answer: A UE shall include the UE additional security capability IE in an ATTACH REQUEST or TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST when it supports one or more EPS NAS security algorithms not representable in the UE security capability IE—i.e., any EPS encryption algorithm EEA8 through EEA15 and/or any EPS integrity algorithm EIA8 through EIA15.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.3.44 (UE additional security capability): the IE indicates EPS encryption and integrity algorithms supported in addition to those indicated by the UE security capability IE. The corresponding ATTACH REQUEST and TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST procedures/message-content clauses require its inclusion when the UE supports EEA8-EEA15 and/or EIA8-EIA15 (commonly cited in clauses 5.4.2.2 and 5.5.3.2, respectively).

results.question: What are the two specific UE capabilities that trigger the inclusion of the UE additional security capability IE?
results.reference: The two capabilities are support for dual connectivity with NR and support for N1 mode.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.4.21, UE additional security capability
results.model_answer: The UE shall include the UE additional security capability IE when it supports either 128-EEA3 (EPS encryption algorithm 3) or 128-EIA3 (EPS integrity algorithm 3).
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2.2 (Attach request message content): the UE additional security capability IE shall be included if the UE supports 128-EEA3 or 128-EIA3.

results.question: Explain the rationale for a UE to provide the UE additional security capability IE.
results.reference: The UE provides this IE to indicate its support for advanced features, specifically either dual connectivity with New Radio or the N1 mode of operation.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.4.21, UE additional security capability
results.model_answer: The IE supplements the legacy EPS UE security capability with the UE's 5GS NAS algorithm support (5G encryption and integrity algorithms). It is relevant for EPS/5GS interworking: an EPS core entity can retain and, where applicable, transfer the UE's 5GS capability information so that a subsequent 5GS NAS security context establishment or mapped-context procedure selects only algorithms supported by the UE. This avoids relying on implicit assumptions about 5GS support and helps prevent selection of an unsupported—or unnecessarily weaker—algorithm during inter-system mobility. The IE is a capability indication, not a request to activate a particular algorithm.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.3, "UE additional security capability" IE, together with the ATTACH REQUEST and TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST UE-procedure clauses in clause 5.5. The IE definition identifies it as carrying 5G encryption-algorithm (5G-EA) and 5G integrity-algorithm (5G-IA) capability information; the relevant procedures specify its use for UE support of 5GS/interworking.

results.question: How should the network handle a lower layer failure that occurs before receiving an IDENTITY RESPONSE during an identification procedure?
results.reference: The network shall abort any ongoing EMM procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.4.6, Abnormal cases on the network side, a) Lower layer failure
results.model_answer: The network shall abort the identification procedure if a lower layer failure occurs before it receives the IDENTITY RESPONSE message. The pending identification transaction is therefore terminated; any later identification attempt requires a new procedure under the normal initiation conditions.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.4.1.2, "Identification procedure initiated by the network": "If a lower layer failure occurs before the network has received an IDENTITY RESPONSE message, the network shall abort the identification procedure."

results.question: What actions must the network take upon the fifth expiry of timer T3470 while supervising an identification procedure?
results.reference: The network shall abort the identification procedure and any ongoing EMM procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.4.6, Abnormal cases on the network side, b) Expiry of timer T3470
results.model_answer: Upon the fifth expiry of T3470, the network shall abort the identification procedure and release the NAS signalling connection.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.4.4.2 (Identification procedure initiated by the network): the T3470 expiry handling specifies that, on its fifth expiry, the network aborts the identification procedure and releases the NAS signalling connection.

results.question: How does the network resolve a collision between an ongoing identification procedure and a newly received ATTACH REQUEST when no attach procedure is pending?
results.reference: The network shall proceed with the attach procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.4.6, Abnormal cases on the network side, c) Collision of an identification procedure with an attach procedure
results.model_answer: The network aborts the ongoing identification procedure and processes the newly received ATTACH REQUEST as an attach request. The outstanding identification exchange is not continued; identification may be initiated again later within processing of the new attach if required.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.3.8.4.2 (Identification procedure — collision with other procedures): when the network receives an ATTACH REQUEST while identification is in progress and no attach procedure is pending, it shall abort the identification procedure and process the ATTACH REQUEST message.

results.question: What should the MME do if an IDENTITY REQUEST message fails delivery due to an intra-MME handover, and the handover procedure subsequently reports a failure while the S1 signalling connection still exists?
results.reference: The MME shall retransmit the IDENTITY REQUEST message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.4.6, Abnormal cases on the network side, h) Lower layers indication of non-delivered NAS PDU due to handover
results.model_answer: The MME shall retransmit the IDENTITY REQUEST message after the intra-MME handover failure is reported, provided that the S1 signalling connection still exists.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.4.4.1 (Identification procedure initiation): when delivery of an IDENTITY REQUEST is unsuccessful due to an intra-MME handover and the handover subsequently fails while the S1 signalling connection exists, the MME retransmits the IDENTITY REQUEST.

results.question: How does the UE choose which EPS bearer context to deactivate when the maximum number is reached and it needs to request a new non-emergency PDN connection?
results.reference: The selection of which specific active EPS bearer context to deactivate is implementation specific, but the UE is prohibited from deactivating an EPS bearer context established for emergency services.
results.model_answer: Before requesting the new non-emergency PDN connection, the UE deactivates a non-emergency EPS bearer context having the lowest retention priority. In practice this means selecting the eligible bearer with the least-preferred ARP priority level (i.e., the numerically highest ARP priority level); an EPS bearer associated with emergency bearer services must not be selected.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.5.1.1 (PDN connectivity — General), in the rule for a UE that has reached the maximum number of EPS bearer contexts and needs a new non-emergency PDN connection. The rule requires release/deactivation of a non-emergency EPS bearer context of lowest priority before the new PDN connectivity request.

results.question: What procedure must a UE perform if it locally deactivates an EPS bearer context in order to request an emergency EPS bearer context?
results.reference: The UE must perform a tracking area updating procedure to indicate the EPS bearer context status to the network.
results.model_answer: The UE shall initiate the UE-requested PDN connectivity procedure, sending a PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST with the Request type set to "emergency" to establish the emergency PDN connection/default emergency EPS bearer context. Local release of another bearer does not substitute for this ESM procedure. If the UE is EMM-DEREGISTERED, emergency access is first obtained through the emergency attach procedure as applicable.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.5.1.2 (UE-requested PDN connectivity procedure), read with clause 5.10 (emergency bearer services). Clause 6.5.1.2 defines establishment of a PDN connection by PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST and includes the "emergency" Request type; clause 5.10 specifies emergency access/attachment behaviour.

results.question: Why would a developer need to consult TS 24.008 when implementing mobile identity handling for NAS?
results.reference: Because TS 24.301 clause 9.9.2.3 for the mobile identity information element explicitly references TS 24.008 clause 10.5.1.4 for the complete definition and encoding details.
results.model_answer: TS 24.301 defines EPS NAS procedures and the EPS-specific use of identities, but it normatively reuses TS 24.008 for the base Mobile identity IE coding. A developer therefore must consult TS 24.008 to correctly encode/decode IMSI, IMEI and IMEISV identities, including the identity-type discriminator, odd/even digit indication, BCD digit packing, length and validation rules. TS 24.301 alone is insufficient for interoperable handling of those legacy/common identity formats; it additionally defines EPS-specific identity handling such as GUTI where applicable.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.3.12, "EPS mobile identity", which normatively refers to 3GPP TS 24.008, clause 10.5.1.4, "Mobile identity", for the relevant mobile-identity coding. TS 24.008 clause 10.5.1.4 specifies the actual Mobile identity IE representation used for identities such as IMSI, IMEI and IMEISV.

results.question: What is the relationship between the mobile identity information element in TS 24.301 and the specification in TS 24.008?
results.reference: The mobile identity information element in TS 24.301 clause 9.9.2.3 is defined by reference, meaning its full technical specification is contained in TS 24.008 clause 10.5.1.4.
results.model_answer: TS 24.301 does not define an independent basic wire format for the EPS mobile identity IE. It normatively reuses the Mobile identity IE encoding specified in TS 24.008, subclause 10.5.1.4, and TS 24.301 defines the EPS-specific applicability and any stated additions/exceptions (notably EPS identity forms such as a GUTI). Thus, TS 24.008 is the base encoding specification, while TS 24.301 profiles/extends it for EPS NAS procedures.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.3.11 ("EPS mobile identity"): the IE is coded/encoded as specified in 3GPP TS 24.008, subclause 10.5.1.4, subject to the EPS-specific provisions stated in TS 24.301.

results.question: Under what condition must a UE include the UE radio capability ID information element in WB-S1 mode?
results.reference: The UE must include it if the UE radio capability ID was requested within the corresponding SECURITY MODE COMMAND message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.21.4, UE radio capability ID
results.model_answer: In WB-S1 mode, the UE shall include the UE radio capability ID IE when it has a valid UE radio capability ID (i.e., an ID associated with its currently applicable radio-capability information).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2 (initiation of the attach procedure): the UE includes the UE radio capability ID IE in ATTACH REQUEST in WB-S1 mode if it has a valid UE radio capability ID.

results.question: How does the UE determine whether to include the UE radio capability ID information element when operating in WB-S1 mode?
results.reference: It checks if the UE radio capability ID was requested in the associated SECURITY MODE COMMAND message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.21.4, UE radio capability ID
results.model_answer: In WB-S1 mode, the UE includes the UE radio capability ID IE only when it has a currently valid, stored UE radio capability ID. The ID is considered usable when it was previously provided/assigned by the network and has not subsequently been invalidated (for example, by a UE radio capability ID deletion indication). If the UE has no stored valid ID, it omits the IE; it does not generate a new ID merely because it is in WB-S1 mode.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2 (ATTACH REQUEST), in the UE radio capability ID IE inclusion rules for a UE operating in WB-S1 mode. Corresponding presence rules are also applied in the applicable mobility-management request procedures, such as tracking-area updating.

results.question: In which operational mode does the requirement for including the UE radio capability ID information element apply, based on the specified condition?
results.reference: The requirement applies when the UE is operating in WB-S1 mode.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.21.4, UE radio capability ID
results.model_answer: The requirement applies when the UE is operating in S1 mode. The UE includes the UE radio capability ID IE only when the stated additional validity/availability condition for that ID is also met.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, the message-content inclusion condition for the "UE radio capability ID" IE (e.g., in the Attach Request/TAU-related message tables): "The UE shall include the UE radio capability ID IE if the UE is operating in S1 mode ..." The operative mode named by the condition is S1 mode.

results.question: What specific message triggers the UE's obligation to include the UE radio capability ID information element in WB-S1 mode?
results.reference: The obligation is triggered by a request within the corresponding SECURITY MODE COMMAND message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.21.4, UE radio capability ID
results.model_answer: The trigger is receipt of an ATTACH ACCEPT message containing the UE radio capability ID IE. In WB-S1 mode, once the UE has received that ID from the MME, it is required to include the UE radio capability ID IE in subsequent applicable NAS requests (notably a later ATTACH REQUEST, where applicable, or TRACKING AREA UPDATE REQUEST) so that the network can identify the UE radio-capability profile.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2 (ATTACH REQUEST message content / conditional IE inclusion). The UE radio capability ID inclusion condition for a UE operating in WB-S1 mode is tied to the UE having received the UE radio capability ID IE in an ATTACH ACCEPT message. The corresponding ATTACH ACCEPT handling is specified in the attach-accept procedure/message-content provisions.

results.question: Under what condition does the network send the Emergency number list IE, and what is the scope of the numbers it contains?
results.reference: The network may send the IE, and if sent, the list contains emergency numbers valid within the same country as the PLMN from which the IE is received.
results.model_answer: The MME includes the Emergency Number List IE in an ATTACH ACCEPT or TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT when it has emergency numbers available to provide and the UE has indicated support for emergency bearer services. The list contains emergency dialling numbers applicable in the country where the UE is currently located (i.e. the serving/visited country), not a universal or home-PLMN-only list; entries can also indicate the associated emergency service category.
results.evidence: Most likely TS 24.301 evidence clause: the ATTACH ACCEPT and TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT procedures specify that, when the UE indicates emergency-bearer-service support and the MME has emergency numbers available, the MME includes the Emergency Number List IE. The Emergency Number List IE definition specifies that it provides emergency numbers applicable in the country in which the UE is located.

results.question: How does the geographic validity of the emergency numbers in the Emergency number list IE relate to the source PLMN?
results.reference: The emergency numbers are valid within the same country as the PLMN from which the IE is received.
results.model_answer: Each emergency number is geographically valid only in the country where the PLMN that supplied the Emergency number list IE is located. Thus, validity is tied to the source/providing PLMN's country, not to the UE's HPLMN or to worldwide use.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, Emergency number list IE clause (most likely clause 10.5.3): "The emergency numbers shall be valid in the country in which the PLMN, from which the emergency numbers are received, is located."

results.question: What determines the country-specific validity of the emergency numbers provided in the Emergency number list IE?
results.reference: The validity is determined by the country of the PLMN from which the IE is received; the numbers are valid in that same country.
results.model_answer: The country-specific validity of emergency numbers in the Emergency number list IE is determined by the Mobile Country Code (MCC) of the UE's current serving/registered PLMN. The list is therefore applicable to the country identified by that MCC, not by the emergency-number digits or the MNC.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.3 (Emergency number list IE): the IE provides emergency numbers applicable to the country in which the UE is currently located; that country is identified by the MCC of the serving PLMN. Related delivery is via the EMM INFORMATION procedure in clause 5.3.7.

results.question: What action must the UE take upon receiving a GUTI REALLOCATION COMMAND message?
results.reference: The UE must delete any previously stored GUTI, store the new GUTI, and send a GUTI REALLOCATION COMPLETE message back to the network.
results.model_answer: The UE shall store the GUTI carried in the GUTI REALLOCATION COMMAND as its native GUTI, then send a GUTI REALLOCATION COMPLETE message to acknowledge successful reallocation. The new GUTI is used for subsequent relevant NAS/RRC signalling.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.4.4 (GUTI reallocation procedure), UE handling of GUTI REALLOCATION COMMAND: the UE stores the received GUTI as its native GUTI and returns GUTI REALLOCATION COMPLETE.

results.question: How does a UE supporting UAS services indicate its identity to the network when requesting a PDN connection for USS communication?
results.reference: The UE provides the CAA-level UAV ID to the network via the protocol configuration options during the attach or UE-requested PDN connectivity procedure.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.3.13.2, Authentication and authorization of UAV
results.model_answer: The UE does not identify itself for USS communication by using the ordinary EPS mobile-identity fields. It requests ESM information transfer in the PDN CONNECTIVITY REQUEST (by setting the ESM information transfer flag). In the subsequent ESM INFORMATION RESPONSE, it provides its UAS-related information, including the UAV/UAS identity, in the Protocol Configuration Options (PCO) IE. This lets the network associate the requested USS PDN connection with the UAV/UAS identity.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 6.10.2.1 (UE-requested PDN connectivity procedure). The UAS-specific text requires a UE supporting UAS services and requesting a PDN connection for USS communication to request ESM information transfer; the UAS-related information, including the UAV identity, is then supplied in the PCO of the ESM INFORMATION RESPONSE. See also the ESM information transfer procedure in clause 6.10.3.

results.question: What is the purpose of a UE providing a USS address via protocol configuration options during certain procedures?
results.reference: The UE provides the USS address so that the network may use this information to discover the USS.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.3.13.2, Authentication and authorization of UAV
results.model_answer: The UE supplies a USS (User Service Server) address in Protocol Configuration Options so that the EPS network can identify/reach the user-service endpoint associated with the UE and apply the requested USS-related service handling. The address is service-selection/routing information; it is not a request for the network to allocate an IP address to the UE. Carrying it in PCO allows the information to accompany the relevant NAS procedure and associated PDN connection setup or update.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 10.5.6.3 (Protocol configuration options), read with the applicable PDN-connectivity/attach or TAU procedure clauses in clause 6.10. PCO is the NAS mechanism for transferring protocol configuration parameters and options between the UE and the network; a USS-address item therefore conveys the UE's service-server endpoint for network processing of that service.

results.question: When can the network initiate a re-authentication or re-authorization procedure for a UE supporting UAS services?
results.reference: The network may initiate the re-authentication or re-authorization procedure as part of a network-initiated EPS bearer context modification procedure, but only after a successful UUAA-SM procedure has occurred.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.3.13.2, Authentication and authorization of UAV
results.model_answer: The network may initiate the UAS re-authentication and re-authorization procedure at any time after the UE has successfully completed an attach procedure or a tracking area updating procedure, provided the UE supports UAS services. The specification does not limit this to a particular ECM state or prescribe a periodic trigger; it is network-controlled.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause titled "UAS re-authentication and re-authorization procedure" (general subclause). It states in substance: "The network can initiate the UAS re-authentication and re-authorization procedure at any time after a successful attach procedure or tracking area updating procedure for a UE supporting UAS services."

results.question: When a normal attach procedure fails and the attach attempt counter reaches 5, what actions must a UE in single-registration mode take regarding 5GMM parameters, and what radio access technologies should it attempt to select?
results.reference: The UE must handle 5GMM parameters (state, update status, 5G-GUTI, last visited registered TAI, TAI list, ngKSI) as specified for a failed initial registration over 3GPP access with counter equal to 5. It shall attempt to select GERAN, UTRAN, or NG-RAN and proceed with appropriate GMM or 5GMM procedures.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.1.2.6, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: On the fifth failed normal EPS attach attempt, a UE operating in single-registration mode shall delete its stored 5GMM parameters and then attempt to select 5GS access: an NR cell or an E-UTRA cell connected to a 5GC.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2.6 (Abnormal cases in the UE for the UE-initiated attach procedure), in the handling of the attach-attempt counter reaching 5. The single-registration-mode-specific requirement directs deletion of 5GMM parameters and selection of an NR cell or E-UTRA cell connected to the 5GC.

results.question: Under what conditions is a UE prohibited from disabling its E-UTRA capability when it selects NG-RAN radio access technology after an attach failure with attempt counter equal to 5?
results.reference: If the 'No E-UTRA Disabling In 5GS' feature is enabled at the UE and it selects NG-RAN, it shall not disable E-UTRA capability. Otherwise, it may disable E-UTRA capability as specified.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.1.2.6, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: The UE shall not disable its E-UTRA capability when it is in the limited-service state. This preserves the UE's ability to obtain emergency service; therefore, even after the fifth failed attach attempt and subsequent selection of NG-RAN, the normal E-UTRA-capability-disable action is barred in limited service.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.1.2 (initiation/abnormal handling of the attach procedure): the attach-attempt-counter handling specifies the action when the counter reaches 5 and NG-RAN is selected, and explicitly states that the UE shall not disable its E-UTRA capability when the UE is in limited service state.

results.question: How should a UE attached for access to RLOS respond upon receiving a paging indication from the network?
results.reference: The UE shall ignore the paging indication from the network.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.6.2.2.1.3, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: The UE shall ignore the paging indication. In particular, a UE attached for access to RLOS shall not initiate the NAS service request procedure, and therefore shall not establish access solely in response to that page.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.6.1.1 (Service request procedure — General): the paging-triggered service-request rule expressly excludes a UE attached for RLOS; such a UE ignores paging indications rather than initiating SERVICE REQUEST.

results.question: Why would a UE ignore a paging indication when it has an ongoing UE-initiated EMM specific procedure?
results.reference: Because the UE is in a state where an EMM specific procedure is ongoing, and the specification requires it to ignore the paging indication.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.6.2.2.1.3, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: The paging indication is ignored to avoid collision with the UE’s already active UE-initiated EMM transaction. Such a transaction is already providing, or attempting to provide, NAS/RRC connectivity and a defined NAS procedure context; acting on paging in parallel could trigger a duplicate or conflicting service-request/connection-establishment action. A paging sent during this interval can be a race/stale indication from before the network observed the UE’s uplink activity. The network can page again or handle the pending downlink service once the UE-initiated procedure completes.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.6.2 (Paging procedure) is the most likely evidence clause. It normatively states, in substance: when a paging indication is received from lower layers while an EMM specific procedure initiated by the UE is in progress, the UE shall ignore the paging indication.

results.question: What action is specified for a UE that receives a paging indication while a service request procedure is in progress?
results.reference: The UE shall ignore the paging indication from the network.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.6.2.2.1.3, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: The UE shall ignore the paging indication if it is received while a service request procedure is in progress.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.6.1 (Paging): "If the UE receives a paging indication while a service request procedure is in progress, the UE shall ignore the paging indication."

results.question: Under what abnormal case related to paging should a UE attached for RLOS access take no action?
results.reference: When it receives a paging indication from the network, it shall ignore it.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.6.2.2.1.3, Abnormal cases in the UE
results.model_answer: A UE attached for RLOS access shall take no action if it receives paging for the CS domain (i.e., the paging CN-domain indication is CS).
results.evidence: Most likely clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.6.1.2, "Paging procedure in the UE" (abnormal handling for a UE attached for RLOS access): paging indicating the CS domain is ignored; the UE takes no action.

results.question: How does the MME respond when it decides to accept a tracking area update for EPS services only in NB-S1 mode, after a UE requested 'SMS only' and supports NB-S1 mode only, and the location update for non-EPS services is not accepted by the VLR?
results.reference: The MME sets the EPS update result IE to 'EPS only', does not indicate 'SMS only' in the Additional update result IE in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message, and includes an appropriate SMS services status value.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.3.2.4A, Tracking area updating successful for EPS services and not accepted for SMS services
results.model_answer: The MME sends a TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT and sets the EPS update result IE to "TA updated for SMS only". It does not indicate a combined TA/LA update, because the VLR did not accept the non-EPS location update.
results.evidence: Most likely normative source: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.3.3, "Tracking area updating accepted by the network". The clause specifies that when the MME accepts the TAU for EPS services only in NB-S1 mode, following an "SMS only" request from a UE supporting NB-S1 mode only, and the VLR has not accepted the non-EPS location update, the MME shall send TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT with the EPS update result IE set to "TA updated for SMS only".

results.question: What triggers the normal or combined tracking area updating procedure for EPS services and 'SMS only' when the tracking area updating attempt counter is equal to 5?
results.reference: When timer T3402 expires after the UE has started it, set the EPS update status to EU1 UPDATED, and entered state EMM-REGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE with the counter at 5.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.3.2.4A, Tracking area updating successful for EPS services and not accepted for SMS services
results.model_answer: Expiry of timer T3402 triggers the UE to initiate the normal or combined tracking area updating procedure for EPS services and “SMS only” when the tracking area updating attempt counter has reached 5.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.3 (tracking area updating procedure initiation/abnormal handling): the retry behavior at a tracking area updating attempt counter value of 5 is governed by T3402; on T3402 expiry the UE initiates the applicable normal or combined TAU procedure.

results.question: During which combined update procedure is the MS identity IE relevant for TMSI management?
results.reference: It is relevant during the combined tracking area and location area update procedure.
results.model_answer: The MS identity IE is relevant during a combined tracking area and location area updating (combined TA/LA update) procedure, including its IMSI-attach variant where applicable. It is used in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT to convey a new TMSI allocated by the MSC via SGs.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 5.5.3.3 (Tracking area updating accept): for a combined tracking area and location area updating procedure, when the MME receives a new TMSI from the MSC, the MME includes the MS identity IE in the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT; the IE contains that new TMSI.

results.question: Under what condition must the network include the Negotiated DRX parameter in NB-S1 mode IE?
results.reference: The network must include this IE when the UE has included the DRX parameter in NB-S1 mode IE in its ATTACH REQUEST message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.1.25, Negotiated DRX parameter in NB-S1 mode
results.model_answer: The network shall include the Negotiated DRX parameter in the NB-S1 mode IE when the DRX value negotiated/assigned by the network differs from the DRX parameter requested by the UE. Its inclusion informs the UE of the network-selected NB-S1 DRX setting; it is not needed when the requested value is retained.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: TS 24.301, NB-S1 mode IE inclusion rule in the relevant EMM accept-message procedure: the network shall include the Negotiated DRX parameter in the NB-S1 mode IE if the negotiated DRX parameter is different from the DRX parameter received from the UE.

results.question: Describe the dependency for the network to provide the Negotiated DRX parameter in NB-S1 mode.
results.reference: The network's provision of this parameter is dependent on a prior action by the UE, specifically the UE including its DRX parameter for NB-S1 mode in the attach request.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.1.25, Negotiated DRX parameter in NB-S1 mode
results.model_answer: In NB-S1 mode, provision of the Negotiated DRX parameter by the network is conditional on the UE having included the DRX parameter IE in the ATTACH REQUEST. The MME then includes the Negotiated DRX parameter IE in the ATTACH ACCEPT to indicate the DRX value selected/negotiated by the network. It is therefore UE-request dependent; it is not sent merely because the UE is operating in NB-S1 mode.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.4.2 (ATTACH ACCEPT message content): the conditional-presence rule for the Negotiated DRX parameter IE specifies its inclusion for an NB-S1-mode UE when the DRX parameter IE was included in the ATTACH REQUEST.

results.question: Under what conditions must the Extended EPS QoS IE be included in a message according to the clause?
results.reference: The IE must be included only if the UE wants to send maximum and guaranteed bit rate values to the network, and at least one of those values exceeds the maximum allowed in the standard EPS QoS IE.
results.model_answer: The Extended EPS QoS IE is mandatory when an EPS QoS IE is present with its QCI field set to value 0. QCI=0 is the indication that the actual (extended) QCI is carried in the Extended EPS QoS IE, rather than in the legacy EPS QoS IE QCI field.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.4.5A (Extended EPS QoS). The clause states in substance: "The Extended EPS QoS IE shall be included in the message if the QCI in the EPS QoS IE is set to 0."

results.question: What triggers the requirement to include the Extended EPS QoS information element?
results.reference: Two conditions must both be met: the UE's intention to transmit maximum and guaranteed bit rate values, and at least one of those values being greater than the limit defined for the basic EPS QoS IE.
results.model_answer: The Extended EPS QoS IE is required when any EPS bearer QoS bit-rate parameter exceeds 8640 kbps: MBR UL, MBR DL, GBR UL, or GBR DL. The trigger is the bit-rate value, not the QCI value alone.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, the "Extended EPS QoS" IE specification in clause 9.9 states in substance: "The Extended EPS QoS IE shall be included if the maximum bit rate for uplink, maximum bit rate for downlink, guaranteed bit rate for uplink, or guaranteed bit rate for downlink exceeds 8640 kbps."

results.question: How does the clause determine when the Extended EPS QoS IE is necessary?
results.reference: It is necessary when the UE needs to communicate bit rate values that cannot be represented within the constraints of the standard EPS QoS information element due to their magnitude.
results.model_answer: The clause uses the QCI value in the EPS QoS IE as the trigger: the Extended EPS QoS IE is required when the QCI field of the EPS QoS IE is set to 0. QCI=0 is the indication that the applicable extended QoS/QCI information is carried in the Extended EPS QoS IE. Thus, its presence is conditionally mandatory under that condition, rather than being selected merely because a bearer has GBR/MBR parameters.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.4.5A, "Extended EPS quality of service". The associated ESM message IE-presence tables specify inclusion of the Extended EPS QoS IE conditional on the QCI in the EPS QoS IE being set to 0.

results.question: What role do the maximum and guaranteed bit rate values play in the inclusion of the Extended EPS QoS IE?
results.reference: The UE's desire to transmit these values, combined with at least one exceeding the standard EPS QoS IE's maximum, mandates the use of the Extended EPS QoS IE.
results.model_answer: The Extended EPS QoS IE is rate-range driven: it shall be included when any EPS-bearer MBR or GBR value (uplink or downlink) exceeds the maximum value representable by the EPS QoS IE, i.e. 10 Gbps. If all MBR/GBR values are representable in the EPS QoS IE, those values do not by themselves require the Extended EPS QoS IE. Thus, the IE extends the encoding range for exceptionally high maximum or guaranteed bearer bit rates; it is not selected merely because an MBR/GBR is present.
results.evidence: Most likely evidence clause: 3GPP TS 24.301, clause 9.9.4.5A, "Extended EPS quality of service" IE — the IE is included when the maximum bit rate for uplink/downlink or guaranteed bit rate for uplink/downlink exceeds 10 Gbps. Related message-specific conditional-presence rules occur in the ESM bearer-context procedures that carry EPS QoS.

results.question: How should the UE proceed when a tracking area update is successful for EPS services only, and the TRACKING AREA UPDATE ACCEPT message contains an SMS services status IE value not treated in clause 5.5.3.2.4A?
results.reference: The UE shall stop timer T3430 if running, increment the tracking area updating attempt counter (unless already 5), then handle based on the counter value. If counter <5, start timer T3411, set EPS update status to EU1 UPDATED, enter EMM-REGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE, and trigger tracking area update for EPS and SMS only when T3411 expires. If counter equals 5, start timer T3402, set EPS update status to EU1 UPDATED, enter EMM-REGISTERED.NORMAL-SERVICE, and trigger tracking area update for EPS and SMS only when T3402 expires.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.3.2.6A, Abnormal cases in the UE, SMS services not accepted
